questions.q: Idera Tennis Club's constitution states that entrance fees paid by new members are to be treated as capital receipts, not revenue income. How should the entrance fees received during the year be treated in the club's final accounts?
o: Credited to the Income and Expenditure Account as ordinary income
Deducted from subscriptions received in the Receipts and Payments Account
Added directly to the Accumulated Fund in the statement of financial position
Shown as a current liability in the statement of financial position
questions.e: Where the constitution classifies entrance fees as capital in nature, they are not passed through the Income and Expenditure Account; instead they are added straight to the Accumulated Fund, increasing the club's long-term reserve.
questions.p: Since the club rules talk say entrance fee na capital money, e no go enter Income and Expenditure Account; instead, dem go add am straight to the Accumulated Fund for the balance sheet.

questions.q: Falconry Social Club's Receipts and Payments Account for the year showed: Subscriptions received ₦300,000; Donations received ₦50,000; Rent paid ₦80,000; Salaries paid ₦120,000; Stationery paid ₦10,000. Additional information: Subscriptions owing (not yet received) at year end ₦5,000; Depreciation on equipment for the year ₦20,000. There were no subscriptions in advance. What is the surplus of income over expenditure for the year?
questions.e: Income = Subscriptions (300,000+5,000 owing)=305,000 + Donations 50,000 = 355,000. Expenditure = Rent 80,000 + Salaries 120,000 + Stationery 10,000 + Depreciation 20,000 = 230,000. Surplus = 355,000 − 230,000 = ₦125,000. Depreciation is a non-cash expense that must still be charged even though it is not in the cash account.
questions.p: Income = Subscriptions (300,000+5,000 wey dem still owe)=305,000 plus Donation 50,000 = 355,000. Expenditure = Rent 80,000 + Salary 120,000 + Stationery 10,000 + Depreciation 20,000 = 230,000. Surplus = 355,000 minus 230,000 = ₦125,000. Even though depreciation no be cash, dem still must charge am.

questions.q: Greenfield Recreation Club runs a bar for its members. During the year: Bar sales were ₦400,000; Opening stock of drinks was ₦30,000; Purchases of drinks were ₦250,000; Closing stock of drinks was ₦40,000; Bar wages paid were ₦25,000. What was the net profit made on the bar for the year?
questions.e: Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Closing stock = 30,000+250,000−40,000 = 240,000. Gross bar profit = Sales − Cost of goods sold = 400,000−240,000 = 160,000. Net bar profit = Gross profit − Bar wages = 160,000−25,000 = ₦135,000.
questions.p: Cost of goods wey dem sell = Opening stock + Purchase minus Closing stock = 30,000+250,000 minus 40,000 = 240,000. Gross profit = Sales minus that cost = 400,000 minus 240,000 = 160,000. Net profit = Gross profit minus bar wages = 160,000 minus 25,000 = ₦135,000.

questions.q: Unity Club received ₦100,000 as life membership fees from a member during the year. The club's policy is to spread life membership fees over 10 years in the Income and Expenditure Account. What amount should be credited to the Income and Expenditure Account for the current year in respect of this fee?
questions.e: Since the club spreads the ₦100,000 life membership fee equally over 10 years, the amount credited each year is 100,000 divided by 10 = ₦10,000. The remaining balance is carried forward as a liability (deferred income) in the statement of financial position.
questions.p: Since the club dey share the ₦100,000 life membership fee for 10 years, the money wey go enter Income and Expenditure Account every year na 100,000 divide by 10 = ₦10,000. The remaining balance go dey carry forward as liability for balance sheet.

questions.q: Which of the following documents normally contains the terms and conditions guiding the operations of a partnership business, including the profit-sharing ratio, capital contributions, and interest on capital or drawings agreed upon by the partners?
o: Trust deed
Articles of association
Partnership deed
Memorandum of association
questions.e: The partnership deed is the legal document that spells out the rules guiding a partnership, such as capital, profit sharing, salaries and interest. The other options relate to companies or trusts, not partnerships.
questions.p: Partnership deed na di paper wey carry all di rules wey go guide di partnership business, like how dem go share capital and profit. Di oda options na for companies or trust, dem no concern partnership.

questions.q: Chidi and Ngozi formed a partnership business but did not sign any written partnership agreement. According to the general rule guiding partnership accounts in the absence of a partnership agreement, how should profits and losses be shared between them?
o: Equally
According to the time each devoted to the business
In the ratio of their capital contributions
In the ratio of 2:1 in favour of the partner who contributed more capital
questions.e: Where there is no partnership agreement, the law assumes all partners share profits and losses equally, regardless of capital contributed or time spent working.
questions.p: If no partnership agreement dey, di law say make dem share profit and loss equally, no matter di capital wey each one bring or di time wey dem spend for di business.

questions.q: Tunde and Bisi are partners in a business. Tunde contributed capital of ₦200,000 while Bisi contributed ₦150,000. Their agreement allows 10% per annum interest on capital before any sharing of profit. What is Bisi's interest on capital for the year?
questions.e: Interest on capital is calculated as capital x rate. For Bisi: ₦150,000 x 10/100 = ₦15,000.
questions.p: Interest on capital na capital multiply by rate. For Bisi: ₦150,000 x 10/100 = ₦15,000.

questions.q: In the appropriation account of Musa and Hassan's partnership, net profit for the year was ₦120,000. Musa is entitled to an annual salary of ₦20,000, and total interest on capital for both partners amounted to ₦10,000. The remaining (residual) profit is shared equally between Musa and Hassan. What is Hassan's share of the residual profit?
questions.e: Residual profit = ₦120,000 - ₦20,000 (salary) - ₦10,000 (interest) = ₦90,000. Shared equally between the two partners gives Hassan ₦90,000/2 = ₦45,000.
questions.p: Di remaining profit be ₦120,000 - ₦20,000 (salary) - ₦10,000 (interest) = ₦90,000. Dem go share am equally, so Hassan go collect ₦90,000/2 = ₦45,000.

questions.q: A partnership's net profits for the last three years were ₦40,000, ₦50,000 and ₦60,000 respectively. If goodwill is valued at two years' purchase of the average profit, what is the value of goodwill?
questions.e: Average profit = (40,000+50,000+60,000)/3 = ₦50,000. Goodwill at two years' purchase = 2 x 50,000 = ₦100,000.
questions.p: Average profit = (40,000+50,000+60,000)/3 = ₦50,000. Goodwill wey be two years purchase = 2 x 50,000 = ₦100,000.

questions.q: At the beginning of the year, Funke's current account had a credit balance of ₦30,000. During the year, she was credited with interest on capital of ₦5,000 and a share of profit of ₦25,000, while she was debited with drawings of ₦15,000 and interest on drawings of ₦2,000. What is the closing balance on Funke's current account?
questions.e: Closing balance = Opening balance + credits - debits = 30,000 + 5,000 + 25,000 - 15,000 - 2,000 = ₦43,000. Current accounts record such day-to-day movements, unlike the fixed capital account.
questions.p: Closing balance = Opening balance + credit items - debit items = 30,000 + 5,000 + 25,000 - 15,000 - 2,000 = ₦43,000. Na current account dem dey use record all dis small-small movements, no be capital account.

questions.q: A partner withdrew a total of ₦60,000 from the business evenly throughout the year for personal use. The partnership charges interest on drawings at 5% per annum, calculated on the assumption that the drawings were spread evenly over the year (average period of 6 months). What is the interest on drawings?
questions.e: Since drawings were spread evenly, the average period used is 6 months. Interest = ₦60,000 x 5/100 x 6/12 = ₦1,500.
questions.p: Since dem spread di drawings evenly, dem go use average period of 6 months. Interest = ₦60,000 x 5/100 x 6/12 = ₦1,500.

questions.q: What is a debenture in company accounts?
o: A reserve created from retained profits
A discount allowed on issue of shares
A loan to a company carrying a fixed rate of interest
A share that carries voting rights
questions.e: A debenture is a form of long-term borrowing by a company. It carries a fixed rate of interest which must be paid whether the company makes profit or not, unlike dividends on shares.
questions.p: Debenture na loan wey company collect, and e dey carry fixed interest rate. Dem must pay the interest even if company no make profit, unlike dividend wey depend on profit.

questions.q: Which of the following is classified as a capital reserve in a company's accounts?
o: Share premium account
Dividend equalization reserve
Retained earnings
General reserve
questions.e: Share premium arises from capital transactions (issuing shares above nominal value), not from trading profit, so it is a capital reserve. General reserve, retained earnings and dividend equalization reserve are all revenue reserves created from trading profits.
questions.p: Share premium na money wey company collect when e sell shares pass the nominal value, e no come from trading profit, so na capital reserve. The other three na revenue reserves wey come from profit.

questions.q: Afrilink Plc issued 50,000 ordinary shares of ₦2 each at a premium of ₦0.50 per share. All the shares were fully subscribed and paid for. Calculate the total amount received by the company from this issue.
questions.e: Each share is sold for the nominal value plus premium: ₦2 + ₦0.50 = ₦2.50. Total received = 50,000 x ₦2.50 = ₦125,000.
questions.p: Each share dem sell am na nominal value plus premium: ₦2 + ₦0.50 = ₦2.50. So total wey company collect na 50,000 x ₦2.50 = ₦125,000.

questions.q: Bayelsa Textiles Ltd has ₦200,000 of 10% debentures in issue. Calculate the amount of annual interest the company must pay to debenture holders.
questions.e: Interest on debentures is a fixed percentage of the nominal value of the debentures. 10% of ₦200,000 = ₦20,000 payable yearly regardless of profit level.
questions.p: Debenture interest na fixed percentage of the nominal value. 10% of ₦200,000 = ₦20,000 wey dem go pay every year, profit or no profit.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes a key difference between preference shares and ordinary shares?
o: Preference shares carry voting rights equal to ordinary shares
Preference shareholders are paid after ordinary shareholders when the company winds up
Preference share dividend fluctuates with profit exactly like ordinary share dividend
Preference shareholders have priority in dividend payment over ordinary shareholders
questions.e: Preference shares usually carry a fixed dividend rate and must be paid before any dividend is given to ordinary shareholders. Ordinary shareholders only receive dividend from what remains, and their dividend varies with profit.
questions.p: Preference shares dey get fixed dividend rate and dem go pay am first before ordinary shareholders. Ordinary shareholders go collect wetin remain, and their own dividend dey change according to profit.

questions.q: A company forfeited 1,000 shares of ₦5 each on which ₦3 per share had been received, including a premium of ₦0.50 per share which had already been fully received before forfeiture. The forfeited shares were later reissued at ₦4 per share, fully paid. Calculate the amount transferred to capital reserve after the reissue.
questions.e: Amount forfeited excluding premium = (₦3 - ₦0.50) x 1,000 = ₦2,500. Discount given on reissue = (₦5 - ₦4) x 1,000 = ₦1,000. Balance to capital reserve = ₦2,500 - ₦1,000 = ₦1,500.
questions.p: Amount wey dem forfeit (without premium) = (₦3 - ₦0.50) x 1,000 = ₦2,500. Discount wey dem give for reissue = (₦5 - ₦4) x 1,000 = ₦1,000. Wetin remain go capital reserve = ₦2,500 - ₦1,000 = ₦1,500.

questions.q: Delta Breweries Plc has 20,000 8% preference shares of ₦10 each and 100,000 ordinary shares of ₦5 each. The profit available for distribution is ₦150,000. After paying the preference dividend in full, the directors share the remaining profit equally among the ordinary shares. Calculate the dividend per ordinary share.
questions.e: Preference dividend = 8% x ₦10 x 20,000 = ₦16,000. Remaining profit = ₦150,000 - ₦16,000 = ₦134,000. Dividend per ordinary share = ₦134,000 / 100,000 shares = ₦1.34.
questions.p: Preference dividend = 8% x ₦10 x 20,000 = ₦16,000. Wetin remain = ₦150,000 - ₦16,000 = ₦134,000. Dividend for each ordinary share = ₦134,000 / 100,000 = ₦1.34.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a general reserve in a company's financial statements?
o: Amount received above the nominal value of shares
Reserve that can only be used to pay dividends to preference shareholders
Reserve created specifically to redeem debentures
Profit set aside for unspecified future use, not tied to any particular purpose
questions.e: A general reserve is part of retained profit that directors set aside for the overall strengthening of the company, not for any specific named purpose. This makes it different from specific reserves such as a debenture redemption reserve.
questions.p: General reserve na part of profit wey directors set aside to make company strong, e no be for any particular purpose. E different from specific reserve like the one wey dem use to redeem debenture.

questions.q: In accounting, what is the main purpose of preparing departmental accounts for a business with several departments?
o: To show total profit of the whole business only
To calculate value added tax payable
To show the profit or loss made by each department
To avoid preparing a trial balance
questions.e: Departmental accounts are prepared so that management can see how much profit or loss each department is making separately, which helps in decision making. It is not about avoiding the trial balance or calculating tax.
questions.p: Dem dey prepare departmental accounts so management go fit see how much profit or loss each department dey make one by one. E no be about trial balance or tax.

questions.q: Chidinma Stores has three departments sharing one shop building. Which basis is most appropriate for apportioning rent and rates among the departments?
o: Floor area occupied by each department
Sales value of each department
Number of customers served
Number of employees in each department
questions.e: Rent and rates are charges for occupying space, so they should be shared according to the floor area each department occupies. Sharing by sales or staff number would not reflect actual space usage.
questions.p: Rent and rates na charge for the space wey dem dey use, so na floor area each department dey occupy go determine how dem go share am. To use sales or staff number no go correct.

questions.q: Zainab Enterprises has two departments, X and Y, sharing the same premises. Department X occupies 600 square metres and Department Y occupies 400 square metres of floor space. Total rent for the year is ₦50,000, apportioned on the basis of floor area. What is Department X's share of the rent?
questions.e: Total floor area is 600 + 400 = 1000 sqm. Department X's share = (600/1000) x ₦50,000 = ₦30,000.

questions.q: When apportioning sales commission paid to salesmen among the departments of a business, which basis is most suitable?
o: Number of employees in each department
Cost of goods purchased by each department
Floor area occupied by each department
Sales value of each department
questions.e: Sales commission is earned based on how much is sold, so it should be shared according to the sales value made by each department. Floor area or staff number does not reflect selling effort.
questions.p: Sales commission dey based on how much dem sell, so e suppose share am based on sales value of each department. Floor area or staff number no relate to selling work.

questions.q: Obi Enterprises, based in Onitsha, sent goods costing ₦200,000 at cost price to its Aba branch during the year. The branch sold all the goods for ₦280,000 cash and incurred branch running expenses of ₦30,000. There was no opening or closing stock at the branch. Using a simple branch account at cost, what is the branch profit for the year?
questions.e: Branch profit = Sales - Cost of goods sent - Branch expenses = ₦280,000 - ₦200,000 - ₦30,000 = ₦50,000. Since there is no stock left, the whole ₦200,000 goods sent is treated as cost of sales.
questions.p: Branch profit = Sales - Cost of goods wey dem send - Branch expenses = ₦280,000 - ₦200,000 - ₦30,000 = ₦50,000. Since no stock remain, all the ₦200,000 na cost of sales.

questions.q: A head office invoices goods to its branch at cost plus 25%, so that the invoice price always includes a mark-up for unrealised profit. During the year, goods invoiced to the branch at invoice price amounted to ₦150,000. What is the amount of unrealised profit (loading) included in this invoice price?
questions.e: Since cost plus 25% equals the invoice price, the loading fraction of the invoice price is 25/125 = 1/5. Loading = 1/5 x ₦150,000 = ₦30,000.
questions.p: Since cost plus 25% na the invoice price, the loading wey dey inside invoice price na 25/125 = 1/5. Loading = 1/5 x ₦150,000 = ₦30,000.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a joint venture in accounting?
o: A temporary partnership formed by two or more persons to carry out a specific business venture and share profits and losses
A branch of a company located in another location
A permanent partnership formed to carry on a continuing business for many years
A department within an organisation handling exports only
questions.e: A joint venture is set up for a specific, short-term business deal, after which it ends, unlike a permanent partnership which continues indefinitely. It is also different from a branch or a department, which are parts of one single organisation.
questions.p: Joint venture na temporary arrangement wey two or more people form just to do one specific business deal, and e go end after. E different from permanent partnership, branch, or department wey be part of one organisation.

questions.q: Public sector accounting can best be described as the process of:
o: recording, classifying and reporting the financial transactions of government and its agencies
recording only the profit made by private limited liability companies
preparing final accounts for sole traders and partnerships
computing personal income tax payable by individual workers
questions.e: Public sector accounting deals with how government ministries, departments and agencies record, classify and report their revenues and expenditures. It is different from private sector accounting which focuses on profit-making businesses.
questions.p: Public sector accounting na how government ministries and agencies dey record, classify and report their money matters. E different from private company accounting wey dey focus on profit.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a normal source of revenue to the Nigerian government?
o: Grants-in-aid from foreign governments or agencies
Dividend earned personally by a private citizen from his own shares in a company
Taxes collected from citizens and companies
Royalties from crude oil and mineral resources
questions.e: Taxes, royalties and grants-in-aid are all recognised government revenue sources. A private citizen's personal dividend income belongs to him, not to government, so it is not government revenue.
questions.p: Tax, royalty and grants na correct government money. But if person get im own shares for company and e dey collect dividend, na im personal money, e no be government revenue.

questions.q: The annual law passed by the National Assembly which authorises the government to spend money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for a given fiscal year is called the:
o: Treasury Circular
Audit Act
Finance (Control and Management) Act
Appropriation Act
questions.e: The Appropriation Act is the annual budget law that gives government legal approval to withdraw and spend money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund. Without it, spending would be unauthorised.
questions.p: Na Appropriation Act be di yearly law wey National Assembly dey pass make government fit spend money from Consolidated Revenue Fund. Without am, government no get permission to spend.

questions.q: Which government fund holds all revenues collected by the Federal Government except those specifically allocated by law to other funds such as the Development Fund?
o: Contingency Fund
Capital Fund
Consolidated Revenue Fund
Sinking Fund
questions.e: The Consolidated Revenue Fund is the main pool into which all federal government revenue is paid, except amounts that the law directs into other special funds like the Development Fund or Contingency Fund.
questions.p: Consolidated Revenue Fund na di main place where all federal government money dey enter, except di ones wey law don already arrange make e go anoda fund like Development Fund.

questions.q: In government accounting, capital expenditure refers mainly to spending on:
o: construction of new roads, bridges and purchase of long-term assets
routine maintenance of office equipment
salaries and wages of civil servants
payment of pensions and gratuities to retirees
questions.e: Capital expenditure is spending that creates or adds long-lasting assets for government, such as new roads, bridges, buildings and equipment that will be used for many years. Salaries, maintenance and pensions are recurrent expenditure.
questions.p: Capital expenditure na money wey government dey spend to build new road, bridge, or buy long-term assets wey go last for many years. Salary, maintenance and pension na recurrent expenditure.

questions.q: The Federal Government of Nigeria approved a total budget of ₦12,000,000,000 for a fiscal year. If recurrent expenditure takes up 65% of the total budget, how much naira is allocated to capital expenditure?
questions.e: Capital expenditure share = 100% - 65% = 35%. So capital expenditure = 35% of ₦12,000,000,000 = 0.35 x 12,000,000,000 = ₦4,200,000,000.
questions.p: Capital expenditure percentage na 100% - 65% = 35%. So e go be 0.35 x ₦12,000,000,000 = ₦4,200,000,000.

questions.q: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) policy was introduced by the Nigerian government mainly to:
o: reduce the amount of tax paid by government parastatals
allow each government agency to keep separate commercial bank accounts for its revenue
consolidate all government revenues into one central account for easier monitoring and control
increase the number of bank accounts operated by ministries
questions.e: TSA brings all government revenue from different ministries and agencies into one unified account at the Central Bank. This makes it easier for government to monitor cash flow, prevent leakages and improve accountability.
questions.p: TSA na policy wey dey gather all government money from different ministries put am for one account for Central Bank. Dis one make am easy to monitor money, stop leakage, and improve accountability.

questions.q: Which method of stock (inventory) valuation assumes that the goods bought first are also the goods sold first, so that the closing stock consists of the most recently purchased items?
o: Weighted Average Cost
Last-In-First-Out (LIFO)
Specific Identification
First-In-First-Out (FIFO)
questions.e: FIFO (First-In-First-Out) means the earliest purchased goods are sold first, so what remains in stock are the newest purchases.
questions.p: FIFO mean say the goods wey you buy first na im you go sell first, so the ones wey remain na the latest ones wey you buy.

questions.q: During a period of continuously rising prices, which stock valuation method will produce the LOWEST value for closing stock?
o: Weighted Average Cost
LIFO
Replacement Cost
FIFO
questions.e: LIFO assumes the most recently bought (higher-priced) goods are sold first, leaving the older, cheaper goods in stock, so closing stock value is lowest when prices are rising.
questions.p: LIFO dey assume say the latest goods wey cost pass na im dem sell first, so the old cheap ones remain for store, dat na why closing stock go small pass.

questions.q: Adaeze's shop had the following stock movements for rice bags in January: Opening stock was 100 bags at ₦50 each. On 10th January she bought 150 bags at ₦60 each. On 20th January she sold 180 bags. Using the FIFO method, what is the value of the closing stock at the end of January?
questions.e: Total bags = 100+150 = 250. After selling 180, 70 bags remain. Under FIFO, the 180 sold come from the oldest stock first: all 100 opening bags plus 80 bags from the new purchase, leaving 70 bags from the ₦60 purchase. Closing stock = 70 x ₦60 = ₦4,200.
questions.p: Total bags na 250, she sell 180, so 70 remain. Under FIFO, the 180 wey she sell na the old 100 bags plus 80 from the new batch, so wetin remain na 70 bags from the ₦60 batch. 70 x ₦60 = ₦4,200.

questions.q: Chinedu's provision store recorded the following for sugar during March: Opening stock was 200 bags at ₦40 each. On 15th March he bought 100 bags at ₦45 each. On 25th March he sold 250 bags. Using the LIFO method, what is the value of the closing stock at the end of March?
questions.e: Total bags = 200+100 = 300. After selling 250, 50 bags remain. Under LIFO, the 250 sold come from the newest stock first: all 100 bags from the March purchase plus 150 bags from the opening stock, leaving 50 bags from the opening stock. Closing stock = 50 x ₦40 = ₦2,000.
questions.p: Total bags na 300, 250 don sell, so 50 remain. Under LIFO, the 250 wey sell na the new 100 bags plus 150 from the opening stock, so the 50 wey remain na from opening stock. 50 x ₦40 = ₦2,000.

questions.q: A trader's stock record for cartons of tomato paste in April shows: Opening stock 50 cartons at ₦80 each, and a purchase on 10th April of 150 cartons at ₦90 each. On 20th April, 120 cartons were sold. Using the weighted average cost method (calculated once before the sale), what is the value of the closing stock?
questions.e: Weighted average cost = (50x80 + 150x90) / 200 = 17,500/200 = ₦87.5 per carton. Closing stock units = 50+150-120 = 80. Closing stock value = 80 x 87.5 = ₦7,000.
questions.p: Weighted average cost = (50x80 + 150x90)/200 = 17,500/200 = ₦87.5 per carton. Wetin remain na 80 cartons (50+150-120). So closing stock = 80 x 87.5 = ₦7,000.

questions.q: Prices of goods have been rising steadily throughout the year. Which statement correctly describes the effect of FIFO compared to LIFO on a trader's reported profit for the period?
o: FIFO gives a lower profit than LIFO because recent, higher costs are matched against sales
LIFO gives higher profit than FIFO because older, cheaper costs are matched against sales
Profit under FIFO and LIFO will always be equal regardless of price movements
FIFO gives a higher profit than LIFO because cost of goods sold under FIFO is based on older, lower costs
questions.e: Under FIFO, the cost of goods sold is based on the oldest (cheaper) stock, so cost of sales is lower and profit is higher during rising prices. LIFO matches the newest (more expensive) stock against sales, giving a higher cost of sales and lower profit.
questions.p: Under FIFO, cost of goods sold dey use the old cheap stock, so cost of sales go small and profit go high when price dey rise. LIFO dey use the new expensive stock, so cost of sales go high and profit go small.

questions.q: A wholesaler's stock card for bags of rice shows: Opening stock 40 bags at ₦100 each, Purchase 1 of 60 bags at ₦110 each, Purchase 2 of 100 bags at ₦120 each. During the period, 150 bags were sold. Using the periodic weighted average method, what is the cost of goods sold?
questions.e: Total cost = (40x100)+(60x110)+(100x120) = 4,000+6,600+12,000 = ₦22,600 for 200 bags, giving an average cost of ₦113 per bag. Cost of goods sold = 150 x ₦113 = ₦16,950.
questions.p: Total cost = (40x100)+(60x110)+(100x120) = 4,000+6,600+12,000 = ₦22,600 for 200 bags, so average cost na ₦113 per bag. Cost of goods sold = 150 x ₦113 = ₦16,950.

questions.q: A supermarket's stock record for cooking oil in May shows: Opening stock 80 units at ₦25 each, and a purchase on 12th May of 120 units at ₦30 each. On 25th May, 150 units were sold. What is the difference between the closing stock value under FIFO and under LIFO?
questions.e: Closing stock units = 80+120-150 = 50. Under FIFO, the 50 remaining units come from the 12th May purchase at ₦30, giving 50x30 = ₦1,500. Under LIFO, the 50 remaining units come from the opening stock at ₦25, giving 50x25 = ₦1,250. Difference = ₦1,500 - ₦1,250 = ₦250.
questions.p: Wetin remain na 50 units (80+120-150). Under FIFO, the 50 units na from the May 12 purchase at ₦30, so 50x30 = ₦1,500. Under LIFO, the 50 units na from opening stock at ₦25, so 50x25 = ₦1,250. Difference = ₦1,500 minus ₦1,250 = ₦250.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa's shop has current assets of ₦240,000 and current liabilities of ₦120,000. What is the current ratio?
questions.e: Current ratio = Current assets ÷ Current liabilities = 240,000 ÷ 120,000 = 2, written as 2:1. This shows the business has ₦2 of current assets for every ₦1 of current liabilities.
questions.p: Current ratio na Current assets divide by Current liabilities = 240,000 ÷ 120,000 = 2, so e be 2:1. Na so dem dey write am.

questions.q: Which formula correctly represents the acid test (quick) ratio?
o: Current assets ÷ Current liabilities
Fixed assets ÷ Capital employed
Net profit ÷ Sales
(Current assets - Stock) ÷ Current liabilities
questions.e: The acid test ratio removes stock from current assets because stock is not quickly convertible to cash. It then divides the remainder by current liabilities to test immediate liquidity.
questions.p: Acid test ratio dey remove stock from current assets because stock no dey quick turn to cash. Na the remaining one dem divide by current liabilities to check if business fit pay quick debts.

questions.q: Chidinma Stores recorded sales of ₦500,000 and cost of goods sold of ₦350,000 for the year. What is the gross profit margin?
questions.e: Gross profit = 500,000 - 350,000 = 150,000. Gross profit margin = (150,000 ÷ 500,000) x 100 = 30%. This shows gross profit as a percentage of sales.
questions.p: Gross profit = 500,000 - 350,000 = 150,000. Gross profit margin = (150,000 ÷ 500,000) x 100 = 30%. Na so dem take find am.

questions.q: Emeka Ventures had sales of ₦800,000 and net profit of ₦96,000 for the year ended 31 December. Calculate the net profit margin.
questions.e: Net profit margin = (Net profit ÷ Sales) x 100 = (96,000 ÷ 800,000) x 100 = 12%. This tells us how much profit is made from every ₦100 of sales.
questions.p: Net profit margin = (Net profit ÷ Sales) x 100 = (96,000 ÷ 800,000) x 100 = 12%. Na how much profit dem get for every ₦100 sales be that.

questions.q: A trader's opening stock was ₦40,000, closing stock ₦60,000, and cost of goods sold for the year was ₦500,000. What is the rate of stock turnover?
o: 8.33 times
12.5 times
10 times
9 times
questions.e: Average stock = (40,000 + 60,000) ÷ 2 = 50,000. Stock turnover = Cost of goods sold ÷ Average stock = 500,000 ÷ 50,000 = 10 times a year.
questions.p: Average stock = (40,000 + 60,000) ÷ 2 = 50,000. Stock turnover = 500,000 ÷ 50,000 = 10 times for the year.

questions.q: Funke Enterprises made credit sales of ₦720,000 during the year. Trade debtors at year end stood at ₦90,000. Using 360 days in a year, calculate the average debtors' collection period.
o: 45 days
30 days
60 days
36 days
questions.e: Collection period = (Debtors ÷ Credit sales) x 360 days = (90,000 ÷ 720,000) x 360 = 45 days. This shows on average how long it takes debtors to pay what they owe.
questions.p: Collection period = (Debtors ÷ Credit sales) x 360 = (90,000 ÷ 720,000) x 360 = 45 days. Na the average time wey debtors dey take pay their debt.

questions.q: A company's net profit before interest and tax is ₦150,000, while its capital employed (total assets minus current liabilities) is ₦1,000,000. What is the return on capital employed (ROCE)?
questions.e: ROCE = (Net profit before interest and tax ÷ Capital employed) x 100 = (150,000 ÷ 1,000,000) x 100 = 15%. ROCE measures how efficiently a business uses its capital to generate profit.
questions.p: ROCE = (Net profit before interest and tax ÷ Capital employed) x 100 = (150,000 ÷ 1,000,000) x 100 = 15%. Na how well the business dey use the capital wey dem get to make profit.

questions.q: A business has a long-term bank loan of ₦400,000 and equity capital (ordinary shares plus reserves) of ₦600,000. What is the gearing ratio, calculated as long-term loan divided by total of loan and equity?
questions.e: Gearing ratio = Long-term loan ÷ (Loan + Equity) x 100 = 400,000 ÷ (400,000 + 600,000) x 100 = 40%. This shows that 40% of the business's long-term finance comes from borrowed funds.
questions.p: Gearing ratio = Long-term loan ÷ (Loan + Equity) x 100 = 400,000 ÷ 1,000,000 x 100 = 40%. E mean say 40% of the long-term money wey business get na loan.

questions.q: Mr. Adeyemi, a tax officer at the Federal Inland Revenue Service, needs the annual accounts of Okpara Plastics Ltd to determine how much company income tax is due. Mr. Adeyemi is best described as a(n):
o: Management accountant of the company
Internal auditor of the company
Internal user of accounting information
External user of accounting information
questions.e: Tax authorities are outside the organisation and only use published accounts, so they are classified as external users. Internal users are those who work within and manage the business directly.
questions.p: Tax officers dey outside di company and dem dey use published accounts, so dem be external users. Na people wey dey work inside di business and dey manage am directly be internal users.

questions.q: Which of these best describes the going concern concept as it relates to the nature of accounting?
o: Accounts must record only transactions that involve cash payments
Accounts should value all assets at their original purchase cost only
Accounts are prepared assuming the business will continue operating for the foreseeable future
Accounts are prepared strictly to satisfy government tax requirements
questions.e: The going concern concept assumes a business will continue trading into the future, which justifies spreading costs of assets over time rather than at break-up value. This is a fundamental assumption underlying the nature of accounting.
questions.p: Going concern concept assume say business go continue to dey run for future, wey make am correct to spread asset cost over time. Dis one na fundamental assumption wey dey guide how dem dey prepare accounts.

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of accounting rather than a reason why it is significant to society at large?
o: It helps government plan and generate revenue through taxation
It helps investors decide whether to buy shares in a company
It provides data for comparing the performance of firms within an industry
It recording, classifying and summarising financial transactions in monetary terms
questions.e: Recording, classifying and summarising transactions describes what accounting actually does, that is, its core function. The other options describe benefits accounting provides to different groups in society.
questions.p: To dey record, classify and summarise transactions na wet accounting actually dey do, meaning na im core function. Di other options na benefits wey accounting dey give different groups for society.

questions.q: The management of Delta Breweries Plc wants to know which product line is least profitable so they can decide whether to discontinue it. This decision mainly illustrates accounting serving as a tool for:
o: Settling disputes with trade unions
Historical record keeping only
Managerial decision making
Legal compliance with company law
questions.e: Using cost and profit information to decide on discontinuing a product line is a planning and control decision made by management. This shows accounting's role in providing data for internal managerial decisions.
questions.p: To use cost and profit info make management fit decide whether to stop one product line na planning and control decision. Dis one show how accounting dey help managers make internal decisions.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes financial accounting from management accounting?
o: Financial accounting is optional for companies while management accounting is compulsory by law
Financial accounting deals only with cash transactions while management accounting deals only with credit transactions
Financial accounting reports are mainly for external users while management accounting reports are mainly for internal users
Financial accounting covers only small businesses while management accounting covers only large companies
questions.e: Financial accounting produces statutory reports like the statement of profit or loss for shareholders, creditors and government, which are external users. Management accounting produces detailed internal reports for planning and control by managers.
questions.p: Financial accounting dey produce statutory reports for external users like shareholders and government. Management accounting invece dey produce detailed internal reports for managers to plan and control.

questions.q: A supplier, Hajiya Fatima, sells goods on credit worth ₦450,000 monthly to Greenfield Stores. Before continuing to supply on credit, she wants to assess the company's accounts to check its ability to pay debts as they fall due. This mainly relates to assessing the company's:
o: Profitability only
Liquidity and creditworthiness
Market share in the industry
Tax liability to government
questions.e: A supplier extending credit is mainly concerned with whether the business can pay its debts on time, which relates to liquidity and creditworthiness. Profitability alone does not guarantee a firm has enough cash to settle short-term obligations.
questions.p: Supplier wey wan give credit want know whether business go fit pay debts on time, and dis one na liquidity and creditworthiness. Profitability alone no mean say company get cash to settle short-term debts.

questions.q: One major significance of accounting is that it helps prevent and detect fraud within an organisation. This benefit is achieved mainly through:
o: Setting selling prices for all goods produced
Preparing advertising budgets for new products
Calculating the market value of competitors' shares
Maintaining proper records and internal control systems that can be checked and verified
questions.e: Proper accounting records with internal controls, such as authorisation and regular checks, make it difficult for employees to steal or manipulate figures without detection. This is why accounting systems are designed with built-in checks rather than relying only on trust.
questions.p: Proper accounting records with internal controls like checks and regular monitoring make am hard for person to steal money without make dem catch am. Na why accounting system get built-in checks.

questions.q: A final year Economics student is studying how national income statistics are compiled using records from thousands of individual businesses across Nigeria. Which significance of accounting does this situation best illustrate?
o: Accounting provides data used in the preparation of national economic statistics
Accounting ensures all businesses pay the same rate of tax
Accounting helps in settling disputes between business partners
Accounting replaces the need for a national population census
questions.e: Government economic planners rely on aggregated financial data from businesses to compute figures such as gross domestic product. This shows how accounting information extends beyond individual firms to support national economic analysis.
questions.p: Government planners dey use financial data from businesses to calculate national figures like gross domestic product. Dis show how accounting info dey help support national economic analysis beyond just one firm.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates the money measurement concept in accounting?
o: A firm separates the owner's personal expenses from business expenses
A firm charges depreciation using the same method every year
A firm values its closing stock at cost or market price, whichever is lower
A firm records only transactions that can be expressed in monetary terms
questions.e: The money measurement concept states that only items that can be expressed in terms of money are recorded in the accounts. Non-monetary matters, such as staff morale or management skill, are excluded.
questions.p: Money measurement concept talk say na only things wey we fit count with money we dey record inside account book. Wetin no get money value, like worker mood or manager brain, we no dey put am.

questions.q: At the end of the financial year, an accountant is preparing the final accounts of a trading business. Stock is valued at ₦240,000 at cost, but due to damage, it can only be sold for ₦190,000. Which accounting concept requires the accountant to report the stock at ₦190,000 rather than ₦240,000?
o: Going concern concept
Prudence (conservatism) concept
Business entity concept
Consistency concept
questions.e: The prudence concept requires that anticipated losses be recognised and assets not be overstated. Since the stock's net realisable value is lower than cost, the lower figure of ₦190,000 must be used.
questions.p: Prudence concept dey talk say make we no overprice our property and make we prepare for loss before e happen. Dem say make we use the lower price of ₦190,000 instead of ₦240,000 because of the damage.

questions.q: A trader buys goods worth ₦500,000 on credit in January and sells all the goods for ₦750,000 cash in March of the same accounting year. Applying the realisation concept, in which month should the profit be recognised?
o: January, when the goods were purchased
Whenever the supplier is paid for the goods
March, when the goods were sold
At the end of the accounting year only
questions.e: The realisation concept states that revenue (and profit) is recognised when goods are sold or services rendered, not when cash is received or goods bought. Since the sale occurred in March, profit is recognised then.
questions.p: Realisation concept dey explain say profit dey show for the exact time wey goods don sell, and not when we buy them or when cash enter hand. Na for March when the goods sell make we recognize the profit.

questions.q: A company's accountant decided to switch from the reducing balance method of depreciation to the straight-line method simply because the new finance manager preferred it, without any genuine business reason. Which accounting concept is most likely being violated?
o: Historical cost concept
Consistency concept
Materiality concept
Going concern concept
questions.e: The consistency concept requires that once an accounting method is adopted, it should be applied consistently from one period to the next unless there is a justified reason for change. Switching methods for personal preference without sound reason breaches this concept.
questions.p: Consistency concept mean say once you choose method, you suppose continue with am every year unless strong reason dey to change am. To just change am because new manager like am dey break the rule.

questions.q: At the end of the year, Chidinma's business had earned ₦60,000 interest on a fixed deposit which had not yet been received in cash, and owed ₦15,000 electricity bill for services already consumed but not yet paid. Under the accrual concept, how should these two items be treated in the final accounts for the year?
o: Both should be ignored until cash is received or paid
The interest should be recorded as income and the electricity bill as an expense for the year
Only the electricity bill should be recorded, since it is a liability
Only the interest should be recorded, since it increases profit
questions.e: The accrual concept requires that income and expenses be recorded in the period they are earned or incurred, regardless of when cash is received or paid. Both the accrued interest income and the outstanding electricity expense belong to the current year's accounts.
questions.p: Accrual concept talk say make we record income and expenses for the year wey dem happen, whether cash don change hand or not. E mean say we must add the ₦60,000 interest and the ₦15,000 electricity bill inside this year account.

questions.q: Mrs Okafor withdrew ₦15,000 cash from her business bank account for personal use. Which source document would be used to record this withdrawal in the bank column of the cash book?
o: Cheque counterfoil
Debit note
Petty cash voucher
Credit note
questions.e: A cheque counterfoil is the stub retained after a cheque is written and shows details of payments made from the bank account. It serves as evidence for cash withdrawals by cheque.
questions.p: Na cheque counterfoil remain for book after person write cheque, e dey show all detail about money wey comot from bank. E dey serve as evidence when person withdraw cash by cheque.

questions.q: A trader receives receipts, invoices and debit notes relating to office expenses paid in cash of small amounts, such as ₦500 for stamps and ₦800 for stationery. In which book of original entry are such small cash expenses first recorded?
o: Bank reconciliation statement
Sales day book
Petty cash book
Purchases day book
questions.e: The petty cash book is used to record small, frequent cash payments such as stationery and postage. It is maintained separately from the main cash book for convenience.
questions.p: Na petty cash book we dey use record small small cash payment like stamps and stationery. We dey keep am separate from main cash book make work easy.

questions.q: Garba's Stores bought goods on credit worth ₦60,000 from Yusuf Enterprises. Before payment, Garba discovered that goods worth ₦8,000 were damaged and returned them. Yusuf Enterprises then issued a document reducing the amount Garba owed. Which document did Yusuf Enterprises issue, and in which book would Garba record it?
o: Debit note; purchases day book
Invoice; sales day book
Credit note; sales returns day book
Credit note; purchases returns day book
questions.e: When a supplier accepts returned goods, it issues a credit note to reduce the buyer's debt. The buyer records this credit note in the purchases returns (returns outwards) day book.
questions.p: If supplier accept goods wey buyer return, dem go issue credit note to reduce the debt. Na inside purchases returns day book the buyer go record this credit note.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the journal proper is sometimes called the 'book of original entry for miscellaneous transactions'?
o: It records transactions that do not fit into any of the specialised subsidiary books
It records only transactions involving the bank column of the cash book
It is used only for recording cash sales and cash purchases
It is used to prepare the trial balance directly without ledger posting
questions.e: The journal proper handles entries such as opening entries, correction of errors, and non-recurring transactions that cannot be entered in the day books, cash book, or petty cash book. This is why it is used for miscellaneous or unusual transactions.
questions.p: Journal proper dey handle things like opening entries, correction of errors, and other matter wey no fit enter normal day books or cash book. Na why dem dey call am book for miscellaneous transactions.

questions.q: A school bookshop in Enugu received an invoice from a publisher for 200 textbooks at ₦750 each, bought on credit. Three days later, 20 of the books were found to be torn and were returned to the publisher. If the publisher accepted the returns, what is the net amount still owed by the bookshop after the return, assuming no other transaction occurred?
questions.e: The total credit purchase was 200 times ₦750 equals ₦150,000, recorded from the invoice in the purchases day book. The 20 returned books worth 20 times ₦750 equals ₦15,000 are recorded in the purchases returns day book, leaving ₦150,000 minus ₦15,000 equals ₦135,000 still owed.
questions.p: Total credit purchase na 200 times ₦750 wey be ₦150,000. When you subtract the 20 returned books wey be ₦15,000, the remaining money wey the shop still owe na ₦135,000.

questions.q: Which of the following documents is the correct source document for recording a cash sale made over the counter of a provision store in Onitsha?
o: Local purchase order
Credit note
Till receipt (cash register receipt)
Debit note
questions.e: A till receipt or cash register receipt is issued at the point of a cash sale and serves as evidence of the transaction. It is used to record the sale directly in the cash book since no credit is involved.
questions.p: Na till receipt or cash register receipt dem dey give person when cash sale happen for counter. E dey serve as proof make person fit record the sale straight inside cash book.

questions.q: Adamu Traders received an invoice from a supplier showing goods bought on credit at ₦120,000, but on checking the delivery note, Adamu found that goods actually delivered were worth only ₦112,000 due to a supplier's overcharge on the invoice. Which document should the supplier send to correct this overcharge, and what effect does it have on Adamu's account?
o: Invoice; increases amount owed by Adamu
Debit note; reduces amount owed by Adamu
Debit note; increases amount owed by Adamu
Credit note; reduces amount owed by Adamu
questions.e: Since the supplier overcharged Adamu, the supplier must issue a credit note to correct the error and reduce the amount Adamu owes. A debit note would be wrong here because it is used when a buyer wants to increase a claim against the seller, not when the seller corrects its own overcharge.
questions.p: If supplier overcharge person, the supplier suppose send credit note to correct the mistake and reduce the money wey the buyer owe. Credit note go bring down the debt.

questions.q: Which pair of source document and corresponding book of original entry is correctly matched?
o: Credit note issued to a customer - Sales returns day book
Cheque counterfoil - Purchases day book
Invoice received for credit purchases - Sales day book
Debit note sent to supplier - Purchases day book
questions.e: A credit note issued to a customer for goods they returned is recorded in the sales returns day book. The other pairings wrongly mix purchases documents with sales books or cash documents with day books.
questions.p: Na credit note wey person issue to customer for returned goods dey enter sales returns day book. The other pairings no correct because dem mix up purchases and sales documents.

questions.q: In the ledger, which of the following best describes the term 'folio column'?
o: A column used to show the running balance of an account
A column used to record the page number of the corresponding entry in another book
A column used to classify accounts as real or nominal
A column used to record the date a transaction occurred
questions.e: The folio column is used to cross-reference an entry with the page or account where its corresponding double entry can be found. It helps in tracing entries between the journal and ledger.
questions.p: Folio column dey help us connect entry to where the other side dey for book. E dey make am easy to trace transaction between journal and ledger.

questions.q: Okonkwo Traders purchased goods worth ₦85,000 on credit from Musa Enterprises. Which of the following correctly shows the double entry for this transaction in the books of Okonkwo Traders?
o: Debit Sales account, Credit Musa Enterprises account
Debit Purchases account, Credit Cash account
Debit Purchases account, Credit Musa Enterprises account
Debit Musa Enterprises account, Credit Purchases account
questions.e: Goods bought on credit increase purchases (an expense, so debited) and create a liability to the supplier (creditor), which is credited. Musa Enterprises is the creditor here, not Okonkwo Traders.
questions.p: When you buy goods on credit, purchases go increase naim make we debit am. Musa Enterprises na supplier, so we go credit their account as liability.

questions.q: A trial balance is best described as a statement that
o: records all cash and bank transactions of a business
shows the final profit or loss of a business for a period
shows the financial position of a business on a particular date
lists all ledger account balances to check the arithmetical accuracy of the books
questions.e: A trial balance is a list of all debit and credit balances extracted from the ledger, prepared mainly to check that total debits equal total credits. It is not itself a financial statement like the profit and loss account or balance sheet.
questions.p: Trial balance na list of all ledger balances wey we use check say debit and credit balance dey equal. E no be final profit or loss statement.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of accounts would both normally have a credit balance?
o: Debtors account and Capital account
Capital account and Sales account
Drawings account and Purchases account
Rent expense account and Cash account
questions.e: Capital represents what the owner has invested and is a liability-type account to the business, so it carries a credit balance. Sales increase profit and are also credited, so both normally show credit balances.
questions.p: Capital and sales accounts normally dey carry credit balance. Capital na money owner put inside business, and sales na income.

questions.q: The ledger account used to record goods taken by the owner of a business for personal use, rather than for sale, is called the
o: Sales account
Capital account
Drawings account
Purchases account
questions.e: When an owner takes goods from the business for personal use, this is treated as drawings, not a purchase or sale transaction, and is debited to the drawings account while purchases (or stock) is credited.
questions.p: If owner carry goods go use for house, we dey call am drawings. Na drawings account we go debit for that one.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains why the ledger is often referred to as the 'book of final entry'?
o: It classifies and summarises transactions already recorded in the books of original entry
It is the first book in which all transactions are recorded before being posted elsewhere
It is used only to record cash transactions of the business
It is prepared after the trial balance to correct errors found
questions.e: Transactions are first recorded in books of original entry such as the journal or day books, and are then posted to the ledger where they are classified under appropriate accounts. This classification role is why the ledger is called the book of final entry.
questions.p: Na book of original entry transaction dey enter first before dem post am to ledger. Ledger come be book of final entry because na there dem dey arrange am well well.

questions.q: The cash book is said to be a book of original entry as well as a ledger account because it:
o: Is used only to record credit sales and purchases
Is prepared only at the end of the financial year by the auditor
Combines the functions of a journal and a ledger account for cash and bank transactions
Records only transactions with the bank for the whole year
questions.e: The cash book records transactions first (like a journal) and also shows running balances (like a ledger account), so it serves both purposes. This dual role is a key feature tested in accounting.
questions.p: Cash book dey work like journal because e dey record transaction first, and e still dey work like ledger because e dey show balance. Na dis two-in-one work make am special for accounting.

questions.q: Emeka bought goods worth ₦8,000 on credit from Hauwa Stores, with terms of 5% cash discount if paid within 10 days. Emeka paid by cheque on the 8th day. What amount should be entered in the discount allowed column of Hauwa's cash book?
questions.e: Discount allowed is 5% of ₦8,000, which equals ₦400. This is the reduction Hauwa Stores gives for prompt payment, recorded in the discount allowed column.
questions.p: Discount allowed na 5% of ₦8,000, wey be ₦400. Na dis amount Hauwa Stores go record for di discount column as di money wey dem give Emeka for quick payment.

questions.q: In a three-column cash book, a cheque of ₦15,000 is withdrawn from the bank for office use. How should this transaction be recorded?
o: Debit cash column and credit bank column with ₦15,000
Debit bank column and credit cash column with ₦15,000
Debit both cash and bank columns with ₦15,000
Credit both cash and bank columns with ₦15,000
questions.e: Withdrawing cash from the bank for office use increases the cash balance and reduces the bank balance, so cash is debited and bank is credited. This is a classic contra entry shown on both sides of the same cash book.
questions.p: If you withdraw cash from bank for office, your cash go increase but your bank balance go reduce. You go debit cash column and credit bank column as contra entry.

questions.q: Tunde's three-column cash book showed total discount allowed of ₦2,500 and total discount received of ₦1,800 for the month of June. At the end of the month, these totals are transferred to the ledger as:
o: Discount allowed debited to discount allowed account; discount received credited to discount received account
Discount allowed credited to discount allowed account; discount received debited to discount received account
Both discounts debited to a single combined discount account
Both discounts credited to the cash account directly
questions.e: Discount allowed is an expense, so its total is debited to the discount allowed account in the general ledger. Discount received is a gain, so its total is credited to the discount received account.
questions.p: Discount allowed na expense, so we go debit am for ledger. Discount received na gain, so we go credit am for ledger account.

questions.q: A trader's three-column cash book showed a bank balance brought forward (debit) of ₦30,000. During the month, cheques received and banked totalled ₦45,000, cheques paid out totalled ₦38,000, and a customer's cheque for ₦4,000 paid in earlier was returned dishonoured. What is the closing bank balance?
questions.e: Closing balance equals 30,000 plus 45,000 minus 38,000 minus 4,000 (dishonoured cheque reverses the earlier receipt), giving ₦33,000. The dishonoured cheque must be deducted because the money was never actually received.
questions.p: You start with ₦30,000, add ₦45,000, minus ₦38,000, and remove ₦4,000 for di dishonoured cheque. Everything come give you ₦33,000 as di final balance.

questions.q: Which of the following transactions would correctly be recorded as a contra entry in a three-column cash book?
o: Purchase of goods on credit from a supplier
Payment of rent by cheque
Receipt of a cheque from a debtor and payment into the business account
Cash sales banked on the same day
questions.e: A contra entry occurs when cash is moved between the cash and bank columns within the same business, such as banking cash sales. This appears on both the debit bank column and credit cash column of the same cash book.
questions.p: Contra entry dey happen when money move between cash and bank inside di same business. Banking cash sales na perfect example because e go show for both sides of di cash book.

questions.q: Ngozi's two-column cash book (cash and bank) showed the following for May: cash balance b/d ₦6,000; bank balance b/d ₦22,000; cash sales ₦9,500 (all banked immediately); rent paid by cheque ₦7,000; cash purchases ₦3,200. What is the closing bank balance at the end of May?
questions.e: Since cash sales of 9,500 were banked immediately, they increase the bank column directly, not the cash column. Closing bank balance equals 22,000 plus 9,500 minus 7,000, giving ₦24,500; cash purchases affect only the cash column.
questions.p: Since dem bank di ₦9,500 cash sales sharp-sharp, e go add to di bank balance. So, ₦22,000 plus ₦9,500 minus ₦7,000 rent go give you ₦24,500.

questions.q: Funke's three-column cash book for March showed the following on the debit side: cash balance b/d ₦7,000, bank balance b/d ₦22,000, cash sales ₦15,000, and a cheque received from a debtor ₦9,000 after allowing him ₦500 discount. What was the total of the discount allowed column for March?
questions.e: Only one discount transaction occurred during the month, the ₦500 allowed to the debtor who paid by cheque. The discount allowed column total for the month is therefore ₦500.
questions.p: Na only one discount happen for that month, wey be the ₦500 wey dem allow debtor wey pay with cheque. So, the total for discount allowed column na ₦500.

questions.q: The main purpose of operating a petty cash book under the imprest system is to
o: allow the petty cashier to borrow money for personal use
replace the need for a general ledger in small businesses
relieve the chief cashier of the burden of recording numerous small payments
eliminate the need for internal control over cash
questions.e: The petty cash book is kept so that small, frequent payments do not clutter the main cash book, leaving the chief cashier to deal with larger transactions. This is the core reason for operating a separate petty cash system.
questions.p: Dem dey keep petty cash book so small-small payment no go choke the main cash book. E dey help the chief cashier face big-big transaction well well.

questions.q: Under the imprest system of petty cash, at the end of each period the petty cashier is reimbursed with an amount equal to
o: the fixed imprest amount, regardless of spending
the total amount actually spent during the period
the balance carried forward from the previous period
twice the total amount spent during the period
questions.e: Under the imprest system, the cashier is restored to the original fixed float by being given exactly what was spent in the period. This keeps the float constant at the start of every new period.
questions.p: Under imprest system, dem go give cashier exact money wey e spend for that period. Na so dem take dey make the money balance reach back the original fixed float.

questions.q: In the petty cash book, after totalling the analysis columns for a period, the sum of all the analysis column totals should equal
o: the fixed imprest amount received at the start of the period
the amount reimbursed by the main cashier the previous month
the closing balance carried down
the total of the payments column in the petty cash book
questions.e: The analysis columns are simply a breakdown of the single total payments column into different expense headings. As a check on accuracy, the sum of the analysis columns must agree with the total of the main payments column.
questions.p: All the analysis columns na just break down of the main payments column. If you add everything together, e must match the total payments amount.

questions.q: Which of the following petty cash entries would normally be posted directly to the main ledger from the petty cash book's analysis columns at the end of the period?
o: Totals of expense headings such as stationery and postage
The closing balance carried down to the next period
The opening balance brought forward
Cash received from the main cashier to restore the imprest
questions.e: Each analysis column total represents a type of expense, and these totals are periodically posted to the relevant expense accounts in the main ledger. Opening balances, restoring cash, and balances carried down are not themselves ledger postings of expenses.
questions.p: Na the totals of expense headings like stationery and postage dem dey carry go main ledger. Dem no dey carry opening or closing balance go ledger as expense.

questions.q: A petty cashier is given an imprest of ₦20,000 on 1st March. By 31st March, vouchers show total payments of ₦13,750. If the firm decides to increase the imprest to ₦25,000 from 1st April, how much cash should the petty cashier receive from the main cashier on 1st April?
questions.e: To restore the old imprest, the cashier needs the amount spent, which is 13750, leaving a balance of 20000 - 13750 = 6250. Since the new imprest is 25000, the cash received must be 25000 - 6250 = 18750, covering both reimbursement and the increase.
questions.p: To reach the new ₦25,000 imprest when you get ₦6,250 for hand, you need ₦18,750. E go cover both wetin you spend and the extra money wey dem add to the float.

questions.q: A key control feature of the imprest system of petty cash is that
o: the petty cashier keeps whatever amount is unspent at the end of the period
vouchers must support every payment before reimbursement is made
the imprest amount is allowed to change without authorisation each period
the main cashier never checks the petty cash book
questions.e: A core control feature is that every payment made by the petty cashier must be supported by a signed voucher before the amount is reimbursed. This prevents misuse of petty cash funds and ensures accountability.
questions.p: Important control be say voucher must cover every money wey you spend before dem refund you. E dey stop people from chop cash anyhow.

questions.q: Okonkwo Ventures fixes its petty cash imprest at ₦18,000. In a certain week, the petty cashier received an extra ₦2,000 refund from a supplier for an earlier overpayment, in addition to making payments totalling ₦9,500. What is the actual cash balance in hand at the end of the week before reimbursement?
questions.e: The cash in hand is found by adding the refund received to the imprest and subtracting payments made: 18000 + 2000 - 9500 = 10500. The refund increases the available cash, so it must be added before deducting payments.
questions.p: You go add the ₦2,000 refund to the ₦18,000 imprest, then minus the ₦9,500 wey you spend. Wetin remain for hand na ₦10,500 before dem refund you.

questions.q: Uche's cash book showed a debit balance of ₦58,000 on 31 July. Comparison with the bank statement revealed that a customer's cheque for ₦15,000 paid directly into the bank had not been entered in the cash book, and bank charges of ₦3,000 had also not been recorded in the cash book. What is the adjusted cash book balance?
questions.e: Start with 58,000, add the direct credit of 15,000 (increases balance), then subtract bank charges of 3,000, giving 70,000.
questions.p: Make you start with 58,000, add the 15,000 wey customer pay directly to bank because e go increase your money, then minus the 3,000 bank charges. E go come give you 70,000.

questions.q: Which of the following items would appear in a bank reconciliation statement but would NOT require any adjusting entry in the cash book?
o: Dividend received by the bank on behalf of the firm, not yet entered in the cash book
Standing order payment made by the bank but not entered in the cash book
Unpresented cheques issued to suppliers
Bank charges deducted by the bank but not entered in the cash book
questions.e: Unpresented cheques are already correctly recorded in the cash book; the timing difference only affects the bank statement side, so no cash book adjustment is needed.
questions.p: Unpresented cheques na those ones wey you don already write for cash book, na just timing difference make bank never clearam. So, e no need any adjustment inside your cash book again.

questions.q: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared starting from the adjusted cash book balance. The following relate to Bisi's account on 31 August: adjusted cash book balance ₦120,000; unpresented cheques ₦25,000; uncredited (outstanding) lodgements ₦10,000. What is the balance as per the bank statement?
questions.e: Starting from the cash book, add unpresented cheques (not yet deducted by the bank) and subtract uncredited lodgements (not yet added by the bank): 120,000 + 25,000 - 10,000 = 135,000.
questions.p: If you dey start from cash book, you go add unpresented cheques of 25,000 and minus uncredited lodgements of 10,000. When you calculate am, 120,000 + 25,000 - 10,000 go give you 135,000.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a usual cause of difference between the cash book balance and the bank statement balance?
o: Bank charges not yet recorded in the cash book
Depreciation charged on the firm's delivery van for the year
Cheques deposited but not yet cleared by the bank
Cheques issued but not yet presented for payment
questions.e: Depreciation is a non-cash accounting adjustment unrelated to bank transactions, so it cannot cause a difference between cash book and bank statement balances.
questions.p: Depreciation na non-cash adjustment for asset and e no concern bank matter at all. Naim make e no fit cause difference between cash book and bank statement.

questions.q: Tunde's bank statement showed a credit balance of ₦96,000 on 30 September. On checking, it was found that: a cheque for ₦18,000 issued to a supplier had not yet been presented, and a lodgement of ₦7,000 made on 29 September had not yet been credited by the bank. What is the balance as per the cash book?
questions.e: Starting from the bank statement balance, deduct the unpresented cheque and add the uncredited lodgement: 96,000 - 18,000 + 7,000 = 85,000.
questions.p: If you dey start from bank statement balance, you go minus the unpresented cheque and add the uncredited lodgement. That means 96,000 - 18,000 + 7,000 go give you 85,000.

questions.q: A dishonoured cheque from a customer, originally recorded in the cash book as a receipt, is later found to have been returned unpaid by the bank. In the bank reconciliation process, this should be:
o: Added to the cash book balance
Deducted from the cash book balance
Added to the bank statement balance
Deducted from the bank statement balance
questions.e: Since the cheque was dishonoured, the earlier receipt recorded in the cash book must be cancelled by deducting it from the cash book balance to correct the error.
questions.p: As bank return the cheque unpaid, you must remove am from your cash book. You go deduct am from your cash book balance because the money no enter at all.

questions.q: Why is a bank reconciliation statement usually prepared on a regular basis by a business?
o: To determine the total value of fixed assets owned by the business
To calculate the profit or loss made by the business for the period
To record all cash sales made by the business during the period
To check and explain the differences between the cash book and bank statement, and detect errors or fraud
questions.e: The main purpose of a bank reconciliation statement is to identify and explain the reasons for differences between the cash book and bank statement balances, helping to uncover errors or fraud.
questions.p: We dey prepare bank reconciliation statement make we fit find out why cash book and bank statement balance no join body, and also to catch any mistake or pocket-fuloko.

questions.q: A trial balance is best described as a statement that is prepared to
o: test the arithmetical accuracy of the double-entry records before preparing final accounts
show the profit or loss made by a business during a trading period
show the financial position of a business at a given date
list all the assets and liabilities of a business
questions.e: A trial balance lists all ledger balances to check that total debits equal total credits, confirming arithmetical accuracy. It is not a financial statement like the balance sheet or income statement.
questions.p: Trial balance na statement wey dem dey use check say debit and credit balance match well before dem do final accounts. E no show financial position or profit like balance sheet or income statement.

questions.q: Adamu bought goods worth ₦18,000 on credit from Bello but the transaction was completely omitted from both the purchases account and Bello's account. Which type of error is this?
o: Error of original entry
Error of principle
Error of complete omission
Error of commission
questions.e: When a transaction is entirely left out of the books, with neither account affected, it is called an error of complete omission. The trial balance will still balance because no entry was made at all.
questions.p: If dem forget transaction completely for book, we dey call am error of complete omission. Trial balance go still balance because dem no enter anything for debit or credit side at all.

questions.q: In preparing final accounts, which of the following errors would cause the net profit figure to be affected?
o: A cheque payment to a supplier was posted to the correct supplier's account but on the wrong side
Discount allowed of ₦2,500 was posted twice to the discount allowed account
A fixed asset purchase was debited to the asset account twice
Carriage inwards of ₦9,000 was wrongly debited to the carriage outwards account
questions.e: Posting discount allowed twice overstates an expense in the income statement, directly reducing the net profit figure wrongly. Errors affecting carriage classification between inward and outward may still distort gross profit only if inward is mistaken for outward, but discount allowed duplication is a clear expense distortion affecting net profit without correction needed elsewhere.
questions.p: If you post discount allowed twice, you don increase expense too much for income statement. Dis one go come reduce net profit figure anyhow.

questions.q: Musa's trial balance failed to agree by ₦5,400, and he posted the difference to a suspense account. On checking, he discovered that the sales day book had been undercast by ₦5,400. Which journal entry corrects this error?
o: Debit sales account ₦5,400; Credit suspense account ₦5,400
Debit suspense account ₦10,800; Credit sales account ₦10,800
Debit suspense account ₦5,400; Credit sales account ₦5,400
Debit sales account ₦2,700; Credit suspense account ₦2,700
questions.e: An undercast sales day book means sales account was understated by 5,400, so sales must be credited with 5,400 to correct it, with suspense debited to balance the correction. This matches the shortfall already recorded in the suspense account.
questions.p: If sales day book undercast, sales account dey short, so you need credit sales account ₦5,400 to correct am. You go come debit suspense account ₦5,400 to clear the suspense.

questions.q: Which type of error occurs when a transaction is recorded using the wrong class of account, for example treating a capital expenditure as a revenue expenditure?
o: Error of principle
Error of original entry
Error of commission
Compensating error
questions.e: An error of principle happens when an entry breaks accounting rules by placing a transaction in the wrong class of account, such as recording capital items as expenses. Error of commission involves posting to a wrong account of the same class, which is different.
questions.p: Error of principle dey happen when person break accounting rule by putting transaction inside wrong class of account, like when you record capital item as ordinary expense. Error of commission different because na to put am inside another account wey belong to the same class.

questions.q: Okonkwo's bookkeeper recorded a purchase of goods worth ₦7,200 as ₦2,700 in both the Purchases account and Bello's (supplier) account. What type of error is this?
o: Error of complete reversal
Error of principle
Error of commission
Error of original entry
questions.e: Since the wrong figure (₦2,700 instead of ₦7,200) was used consistently in both accounts, this is an error of original entry. The trial balance still balances because both sides were equally understated.
questions.p: Because dem use the wrong figure of ₦2,700 instead of ₦7,200 inside both accounts, na error of original entry be that. Trial balance still go balance because both sides reduce by the same amount.

questions.q: In Chidinma's ledger, a total of ₦12,000 was posted to the debit side of the Sales account instead of the credit side. What effect will this have on the trial balance?
o: The trial balance will disagree by ₦12,000
The trial balance will disagree by ₦6,000
The trial balance will still agree
The trial balance will disagree by ₦24,000
questions.e: Posting a credit entry to the debit side means the debit column is overstated by ₦12,000 while the credit column loses ₦12,000 it should have had, creating a total difference of ₦12,000 + ₦12,000 = ₦24,000. This is called an error of complete reversal.
questions.p: If you put credit entry for debit side, debit column go surplus by ₦12,000 and credit column go lose ₦12,000 wey e suppose get. When you join the two together, na ₦12,000 plus ₦12,000 wey give you ₦24,000 difference.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the nature of a suspense account?
o: It is a temporary account used to balance the trial balance until errors are located and corrected
It is a permanent account that appears in the final published accounts every year
It is an account used to record all cash transactions of a business
It is an account that shows the total capital contributed by the owner of a business
questions.e: A suspense account is only a temporary holding account opened when a trial balance fails to balance, so that the accountant can proceed with preparing accounts while searching for the error. Once the error is found, it is corrected and the suspense account is closed.
questions.p: Suspense account na temporary account wey dem dey open only when trial balance no balance, so accountant fit continue work while dem dey find the error. Once dem see the error, dem go close the suspense account.

questions.q: A trader's trial balance disagreed and a suspense account was opened. Later it was discovered that a discount allowed of ₦1,500 had been correctly entered in the cash book but had not been posted to the Discount Allowed account at all. Which journal entry correctly corrects this error?
o: Debit Cash Book ₦1,500; Credit Discount Allowed account ₦1,500
Debit Discount Allowed account ₦1,500; Credit Suspense account ₦1,500
Debit Suspense account ₦1,500; Credit Discount Allowed account ₦1,500
Debit Discount Allowed account ₦1,500; Credit Cash Book ₦1,500
questions.e: Since the cash book was already correctly entered but the Discount Allowed account was never posted, the correction is to debit Discount Allowed (since it is an expense that reduces profit) and credit the Suspense account to balance the missing side. This closes the gap caused by the one-sided omission.
questions.p: Since cash book correct but dem forget Discount Allowed account, you need to debit Discount Allowed account ₦1,500 and credit Suspense account ₦1,500. This one go clear the missing one-sided error.

questions.q: Which one of the following errors is correctly classified as an error of commission?
o: Recording the purchase of a delivery motorcycle as an ordinary motor running expense
Posting a payment correctly received from Grace but wrongly entered in Gloria's account, another customer
Failing to record a cash sale of ₦3,000 anywhere in the books
Recording a sale of ₦4,000 on both sides of the ledger as ₦400
