questions.e: An error of commission occurs when an entry is posted to the wrong personal account of the correct class, such as crediting Gloria instead of Grace for a payment received. The other options describe errors of principle, omission, and original entry respectively.
questions.p: Error of commission dey happen when you post transaction to wrong personal account inside the correct class, like putting money inside Gloria account instead of Grace. The other options na error of principle, omission, and original entry.

questions.q: After extracting his trial balance, Emeka found that a sale of goods for ₦9,000 to a customer, Tunde, had been correctly entered in the Sales account but had never been posted to Tunde's account. Before this error is found, in which financial statement would a suspense account balance most likely appear?
o: In the Statement of Profit or Loss as an expense
In the Trading account as part of cost of sales
In the Statement of Financial Position (Balance Sheet) until the error is corrected
In the Cash Flow Statement under financing activities
questions.e: A suspense account balance is a temporary difference that is shown in the Statement of Financial Position, usually as a debit balance similar to an asset, until the underlying error causing it is located and corrected. It does not affect the Trading or Profit or Loss account directly.
questions.p: Suspense account balance na temporary thing wey dey show for Statement of Financial Position until dem find and correct the error. E no dey affect Trading or Profit or Loss account directly.

questions.q: In preparing the final accounts of a sole trader, carriage inwards is treated by:
o: Deducting it from closing stock in the balance sheet
Deducting it from sales in the trading account
Adding it to purchases in the trading account
Adding it to selling expenses in the profit and loss account
questions.e: Carriage inwards is the cost of bringing goods into the business, so it forms part of the cost of purchases and is added to purchases in the trading account. Carriage outwards, on the other hand, is a selling expense charged to the profit and loss account.
questions.p: Carriage inwards na money wey you pay to bring goods enter your shop, so e dey join cost of purchases. You go add am for trading account. Carriage outwards na different thing, na selling expense wey dey go profit and loss account.

questions.q: A sole trader's trial balance showed a debit balance on the rent account of ₦36,000 for the year. At the year end, rent of ₦9,000 had been paid in advance for the next accounting period. How should this be treated in the final accounts?
o: Show ₦45,000 as an expense in profit and loss account and ignore the ₦9,000
Show ₦36,000 as an expense in profit and loss account and ₦9,000 as a current liability
Show ₦9,000 as an expense in profit and loss account and ₦27,000 as a current asset
Show ₦27,000 as an expense in profit and loss account and ₦9,000 as a current asset
questions.e: Since ₦9,000 relates to the next period, it is a prepayment and must be removed from this year's expense, leaving 36,000 - 9,000 = 27,000 charged to profit and loss account. The prepaid amount of 9,000 is shown as a current asset in the balance sheet because it represents a future benefit.
questions.p: Because 9,000 na money wey you pay for next year, you must remove am from this year expense. 36,000 minus 9,000 give you 27,000 for profit and loss. That 9,000 na current asset for balance sheet because e be benefit for future.

questions.q: Which of the following items would appropriately appear under current liabilities in the balance sheet of a sole trader?
o: Trade creditors owed for goods supplied
Cash in hand
Motor vehicle at cost
Closing stock of unsold goods
questions.e: Trade creditors represent amounts the business owes to suppliers for goods bought on credit and must be settled within a short period, making them a current liability. Motor vehicle, closing stock and cash are all assets, not liabilities.
questions.p: Trade creditors na people wey you owe money for goods wey you buy on credit. You must pay dem back quick, so e be current liability. Motor vehicle, stock and cash na assets, no be liability.

questions.q: Bola, a sole trader, provided the following figures for the year: Net profit before adjustment ₦120,000; a debt of ₦8,000 owed by a customer is now considered irrecoverable and must be written off; provision for doubtful debts is to be created at 5% on the remaining debtors of ₦152,000. What is the adjusted net profit?
questions.e: First deduct the bad debt of 8,000 from the net profit, leaving 112,000. Then create a provision for doubtful debts of 5% of 152,000, which is 7,600, and deduct it from 112,000 to get 104,400.
questions.p: First, remove the 8,000 bad debt from 120,000 to get 112,000. Then calculate 5% of 152,000 which be 7,600 as provision for doubtful debts. Subtract that 7,600 from 112,000 to get 104,400.

questions.q: In the final accounts of a sole trader, the purpose of preparing a profit and loss account, after the trading account, is mainly to:
o: Determine the value of closing stock at year end
Determine the net profit or net loss after charging operating expenses against gross profit
Show the total sales and cost of goods sold for the period
Show the financial position of the business at a point in time
questions.e: The profit and loss account takes the gross profit from the trading account and deducts all other operating expenses, such as rent, salaries and depreciation, to arrive at net profit or net loss. Financial position is shown by the balance sheet, not the profit and loss account.
questions.p: Profit and loss account dey take gross profit from trading account and remove all operating expenses like rent and salary. This one go show you whether you make net profit or net loss. Balance sheet na im dey show financial position.

questions.q: At the end of the year, a sole trader's trial balance showed closing stock already adjusted into the trading account. However, it was later discovered that goods costing ₦18,000, sent to a customer on sale or return basis, had wrongly been included in both sales (at ₦25,000) and excluded from closing stock. How will correcting this error affect the final accounts?
o: Increase gross profit by ₦7,000
Reduce net profit by ₦18,000 only
Reduce sales by ₦25,000 and increase closing stock by ₦18,000
No adjustment is needed since goods were sent to the customer
questions.e: Since the goods were only sent on a sale or return basis and not actually sold, the ₦25,000 must be removed from sales and the ₦18,000 cost of those goods must be added back to closing stock. This corrects both the trading account and the balance sheet figures.
questions.p: Since the goods no be real sale, you must remove 25,000 from sales account. You also need to add the 18,000 cost back to your closing stock. This one go make your account correct.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the double entry treatment when a sole trader takes goods from the business stock for his personal use, without making any payment?
o: Debit sales account and credit drawings account
Debit purchases account and credit drawings account
Debit drawings account and credit sales account
Debit drawings account and credit purchases account
questions.e: Goods taken by the owner for personal use reduce the goods available for sale, so purchases account is credited to reduce it, while drawings account is debited to record the owner's withdrawal. This ensures the trading account reflects only goods meant for resale to customers.
questions.p: When owner carry goods for personal use, e dey reduce the goods wey dey for shop. You go credit purchases account to reduce am and debit drawings account. This one show say the goods no be for sale again.

questions.q: Ngozi runs a trading business and pays insurance premiums in advance. On 1 January, the prepaid insurance brought forward from the previous year was ₦15,000. During the year, she paid ₦90,000 for insurance. At the end of the year, ₦20,000 of this payment relates to the following year. What amount should be charged to the income statement for insurance for the year?
questions.e: The amount used in the year equals opening prepayment plus payments made minus the new closing prepayment: 15,000 + 90,000 - 20,000 = 85,000. This gives the true expense for the period.
questions.p: To find the correct insurance expense, you go add the opening prepayment to the money wey you pay, then minus the closing prepayment. E mean say 15,000 + 90,000 - 20,000 go give you ₦85,000.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an accrued revenue at the end of an accounting year?
o: Subscription received for the following year
Rent received in advance from a tenant
Commission earned but not yet received from a customer
Interest paid in advance on a loan
questions.e: Accrued revenue is income that has been earned during the year but not yet received in cash by the year end. Commission earned but unpaid fits this description exactly.
questions.p: Accrued revenue na money wey you don work for or earn finish, but cash never enter hand before year end. Commission wey person earn but dem never pay am fit this description well well.

questions.q: A trader's financial year ends on 31 December. On 31 December, wages for the last week of the year amounting to ₦18,000 had not yet been paid to workers. How should this amount be treated in the final accounts for that year?
o: Added to wages in the income statement and shown as a current asset
Deducted from wages in the income statement and shown as a current liability
Deducted from wages in the income statement and shown as a current asset
Added to wages in the income statement and shown as a current liability
questions.e: Unpaid wages at year end are an accrued expense, meaning the full cost has been incurred but not paid. It must be added to the expense in the income statement and shown as a current liability in the statement of financial position.
questions.p: Wages wey dem never pay for year end na accrued expense, so you must add am to wages inside income statement. Because na debt wey you owe workers, you go show am as current liability for statement of financial position.

questions.q: In the books of Danjuma Enterprises, trade debtors stood at ₦800,000 before any adjustment. It was discovered that a debtor, Bello, who owed ₦30,000, had been declared bankrupt and would pay nothing. After writing off this debt, a provision for doubtful debts of 2% is to be created on the remaining debtors. What is the amount of the provision for doubtful debts?
questions.e: After writing off the bad debt, debtors reduce to 800,000 - 30,000 = 770,000. The provision is then 2% of 770,000 = 15,400.
questions.p: First, you go remove the bad debt from total debtors: 800,000 - 30,000 wey remain ₦770,000. Then, you calculate 2% provision on the remaining amount, wey be 2/100 x 770,000 = ₦15,400.

questions.q: Kabiru Stores paid ₦240,000 as rent covering 12 months from 1 April of the current year to 31 March of the following year. If the accounting year ends on 31 December, what amount of prepaid rent should appear in the statement of financial position at year end?
questions.e: Monthly rent is 240,000 divided by 12 = 20,000. From January to March of the following year (3 months) is unused at year end, so prepaid rent is 20,000 x 3 = 60,000.
questions.p: Since the rent na ₦240,000 for 12 months, every month rent na ₦20,000. Dem don pay advance for January to March of the next year, meaning 3 months be prepaid, so 20,000 x 3 = ₦60,000.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why a provision for depreciation account is maintained separately from the asset account in the ledger?
o: To show the original cost of the asset and the total depreciation charged separately
To record the cash received from the sale of the asset
To increase the value of the asset over time
To avoid recording the asset in the balance sheet
questions.e: Keeping the two accounts separate allows the historical cost of the asset to remain unchanged while accumulated depreciation is tracked on its own account. The net book value is found by subtracting the provision for depreciation from the cost.
questions.p: Make we keep di two accounts separate so dat di original cost of di asset go dey intact while we dey track total depreciation for hin own account. Na to minus di provision for depreciation from di cost you go take see di net book value.

questions.q: A company's policy is to charge a full year's depreciation in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. A machine bought on 1 January 2019 for ₦800,000 is depreciated at 20% per annum on cost using the straight line method. If the machine is sold on 30 June 2022, how many years of depreciation would have been charged on it by the date of disposal?
o: 5 years
4 years
2 years
3 years
questions.e: Since no depreciation is charged in the year of disposal, only 2019, 2020 and 2021 attract a full year's charge, giving 3 years in total. This means accumulated depreciation would be 3 x 20% x 800,000 = 480,000.
questions.p: Because company policy talk say make we no charge depreciation for di year wey we sell am, na only 2019, 2020 and 2021 go carry full year depreciation, wey make am 3 years in total. Dis mean say accumulated depreciation na 3 x 20% x 800,000 = 480,000.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a recognised method of calculating depreciation taught in financial accounting?
o: Reducing balance method
Revaluation method
Market speculation method
Straight line method
questions.e: Straight line, reducing balance and revaluation are standard recognised depreciation methods. Market speculation method does not exist as an accounting method for depreciation.
questions.p: Straight line, reducing balance and revaluation na proper depreciation methods wey dem dey teach. Market speculation method no even exist for accounting at all.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct accounting entry to record the sale of a non-current asset for cash, assuming the disposal account has already received the cost and accumulated depreciation transfers?
o: Debit Disposal account, Credit Cash
Debit Cash, Credit Disposal account
Debit Depreciation account, Credit Cash
Debit Asset account, Credit Cash
questions.e: When cash is received from selling an asset, cash increases, so it is debited, while the disposal account is credited to close off the proceeds against the cost and accumulated depreciation already posted there. This correctly completes the disposal account workings.
questions.p: If cash enter from selling asset, cash dey increase, so na debit we go give cash, and we go credit disposal account. Dis one go make di disposal account balance correct.

questions.q: Why is depreciation regarded as a non-cash expense in the preparation of financial statements?
o: Because it does not involve an actual outflow of cash when charged
Because it is only recorded when the asset is sold
Because it represents money borrowed to buy the asset
Because it increases the cash balance of the business
questions.e: Depreciation simply spreads the cost of an asset over its useful life in the income statement without any cash leaving the business at the point the expense is recorded. The actual cash outflow occurred earlier, when the asset was originally purchased.
questions.p: Depreciation just dey spread asset cost over hin useful life without any physical cash leaving di pocket when you dey record am. Na dat time wey you buy di asset before, cash bin commot.

questions.q: A delivery tricycle costing ₦250,000 was depreciated using the reducing balance method at 20% per annum. What is its net book value at the end of the second year?
questions.e: After year one, book value is 250,000 - 20% of 250,000 = 200,000. After year two, book value is 200,000 - 20% of 200,000 = 160,000.
questions.p: For year one, book value na 250,000 minus 20% of 250,000, wey give us 200,000. For year two, book value go come be 200,000 minus 20% of 200,000, wey be ₦160,000.

questions.q: Control accounts are often described as a 'master ledger' because they summarise the transactions of a group of personal accounts. Which of these best describes the main source of entries posted into the Sales Ledger Control Account?
o: Entries made directly from the bank statement
Balances extracted from the Purchases Ledger only
Totals from the books of original entry (journals) relating to debtors
Individual postings copied from every debtor's personal account
questions.e: Control accounts are written up from totals in the books of original entry (such as the sales day book, cash book and returns inwards book), not from individual personal accounts. This keeps the control account as a summary check on the sales ledger.
questions.p: Control account dey take totals from books of original entry like sales day book, no be say dem dey copy am one by one from everybody account. E dey help us check weda sales ledger balance correct.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct reason for preparing self-balancing ledgers in a business?
o: To replace the need for preparing a statement of financial position
To allow the trial balance of each ledger to be extracted independently without needing the other ledgers
To ensure that only cash transactions are recorded in the books
To eliminate the need for subsidiary books such as the sales day book
questions.e: In a self-balancing ledger system, each ledger (sales, purchases, general) contains an adjustment or control account so that a trial balance can be extracted from that ledger alone. This localises errors to a particular ledger, making it easier to detect where a mistake occurred.
questions.p: Self-balancing ledger system dey allow trial balance for each ledger make e stand on im own without needing other ledgers. E dey help us locate mistake quick quick for dat particular ledger.

questions.q: A trader's Sales Ledger Control Account for the month of March showed: opening debit balance ₦72,000; credit sales ₦250,000; cash received from debtors ₦210,000; discount allowed ₦8,000; returns inwards ₦12,000. What is the closing balance on the control account?
questions.e: Closing balance = (72000 + 250000) - (210000 + 8000 + 12000) = 322000 - 230000 = ₦92,000. Debit side items (opening balance and sales) are added while credit side items (cash, discount allowed, returns) are deducted.
questions.p: To find closing balance, you go add opening balance ₦72,000 and credit sales ₦250,000 to get ₦322,000, then minus cash ₦210,000, discount ₦8,000 and returns ₦12,000. Dat one go give you ₦92,000.

questions.q: A debtor, Mallam Yusuf, owed a business ₦25,000. During the month, the business supplied him goods on credit worth ₦40,000, but he returned damaged goods worth ₦5,000 and his account was also credited with a set-off of ₦10,000 against an amount the business owed him as a supplier. What balance remains on Mallam Yusuf's account?
questions.e: Balance = 25000 + 40000 - 5000 - 10000 = ₦50,000. The opening debt and new credit sales increase the balance, while returns and the contra set-off against the Purchases Ledger reduce it.
questions.p: You go start with ₦25,000, add ₦40,000 for goods wey dem supply, then minus ₦5,000 for goods wey return and ₦10,000 for contra set-off. E go remain ₦50,000 for im account.

questions.q: Which of the following items would normally appear in a Purchases Ledger Control Account but would NOT appear in a Sales Ledger Control Account?
o: Bad debts written off
Cash received from customers
Discount allowed to customers
Discount received from suppliers
questions.e: Discount received relates to amounts owed to suppliers, so it appears in the Purchases Ledger Control Account, not the Sales Ledger Control Account. Bad debts, discount allowed and cash received from customers all relate to debtors and belong in the Sales Ledger Control Account.
questions.p: Discount received na for people wey we owe, na im make e dey Purchases Ledger Control Account. Discount allowed and cash received na for customers wey dey Sales Ledger Control Account.

questions.q: A business's Sales Ledger Control Account and the total of individual balances in the Sales Ledger did not agree at the end of the year. Which of the following errors would cause such a disagreement?
o: A credit sale of ₦15,000 to a customer was correctly entered in the Sales Day Book but posted to the customer's account as ₦1,500
A credit sale of ₦15,000 was completely omitted from both the Sales Day Book and the customer's account
The total of the Sales Day Book was correctly transferred to both the control account and all customer accounts
A cheque received from a customer was correctly recorded in both the cash book and the customer's account
questions.e: Since the control account is posted from the Sales Day Book total (₦15,000), it would be correct, but the individual customer account would only show ₦1,500, causing the sum of individual balances to differ from the control account. Errors of complete omission or errors affecting both equally would not cause a disagreement.
questions.p: If control account get correct total from Sales Day Book but customer own record small amount like ₦1,500 instead of ₦15,000, the two totals no go match. Complete omission no dey cause disagreement because e miss for both sides.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'work-in-progress' in a manufacturing account?
o: Raw materials that have not yet entered the production process
Finished goods transferred from the factory to the warehouse
Goods that have been completed and are ready for sale
Goods that are partly completed at the end of the accounting period
questions.e: Work-in-progress refers to partly finished goods still in the production process at the end of the period. It is neither raw material nor fully finished goods.
questions.p: Work-in-progress mean goods wey never finish for production process as accounting period dey end. E no be raw material and e no be finished goods yet.

questions.q: In a manufacturing account, factory overheads consist mainly of:
o: Carriage outwards on finished goods sold to customers
Cost of raw materials purchased during the year
Indirect factory costs such as factory rent, depreciation of factory machinery and factory supervisors' salaries
Wages paid directly to workers who make the product
questions.e: Factory overheads are indirect costs incurred in running the factory, like rent, depreciation and supervision, not direct material or direct labour costs.
questions.p: Factory overheads na all those indirect costs wey we dey spend for factory, like rent, depreciation and supervision. E no include direct material or direct labour cost.

questions.q: In the final accounts of a manufacturing business, where is the cost of production of finished goods transferred to?
o: Credit side of the trading account and debit side of the manufacturing account
Credit side of the manufacturing account and debit side of the trading account
Debit side of the manufacturing account and credit side of the balance sheet
Debit side of the profit and loss account only
questions.e: The cost of production is a closing figure in the manufacturing account (credited there) and then brought down to the debit side of the trading account as the cost of goods manufactured.
questions.p: We go credit the cost of production for manufacturing account, then carry am come debit side of trading account as cost of goods manufactured.

questions.q: Fatima Foods Ltd provided the following for the year: direct materials consumed ₦300,000; direct labour ₦180,000; direct expenses ₦20,000; factory overheads ₦150,000; opening work-in-progress ₦30,000; closing work-in-progress ₦50,000. The finished goods were then transferred to the warehouse at cost plus 20% mark-up for internal trading purposes. What is the transfer value of the finished goods to the trading account?
questions.e: Prime cost = 300,000+180,000+20,000 = 500,000. Add factory overheads 150,000 = 650,000. Add opening WIP 30,000 less closing WIP 50,000 gives cost of production 630,000. Transfer value with 20% mark-up = 630,000 x 1.20 = 756,000.
questions.p: Prime cost plus factory overheads plus opening WIP minus closing WIP give us cost of production as ₦630,000. When we add 20% mark-up, the final transfer value enter ₦756,000.

questions.q: In the accounts of not-for-profit organisations, which term is used instead of 'profit and loss account' to show whether the organisation has a surplus or a deficit for the year?
o: Statement of Affairs
Income and Expenditure Account
Receipts and Payments Account
Appropriation Account
questions.e: The Income and Expenditure Account is the equivalent of the profit and loss account for non-trading concerns. It shows surplus or deficit of income over expenditure for the year.
questions.p: Na Income and Expenditure Account dem dey use instead of profit and loss account for non-trading organization. E dey show whether the place make surplus or deficit for that year.

questions.q: Obudu Welfare Club's Receipts and Payments Account showed rent paid of ₦60,000 during the year. At the start of the year, rent owing was ₦8,000, and at the end of the year, rent owing was ₦5,000. What amount should appear as rent expense in the Income and Expenditure Account?
questions.e: Rent for the year equals cash paid minus opening accrual plus closing accrual, that is 60,000 minus 8,000 plus 5,000, which equals 57,000. This adjusts cash paid to the actual expense incurred during the year.
questions.p: To find the correct rent, you go minus the opening arrears from the cash wey you pay, then add the closing arrears. So, 60,000 minus 8,000 plus 5,000 go give you ₦57,000.

questions.q: In preparing the final accounts of a not-for-profit organisation, the balance brought down on the Receipts and Payments Account at the start of the year represents what?
o: Opening cash and bank balance
Opening accumulated fund
Opening subscriptions in arrears
Opening value of fixed assets
questions.e: The Receipts and Payments Account is simply a summary of the cash book, so its opening balance is the cash and bank balance brought forward from the previous year. It is not related to capital or fixed assets.
questions.p: Receipts and Payments Account na just cash book summary. E mean say any balance wey come down for front of the account na cash and bank balance from last year.

questions.q: Why is a Statement of Affairs, rather than a formal Balance Sheet, often used to find the opening accumulated fund of a not-for-profit organisation?
o: Because members do not need to know the value of the organisation's assets
Because subscriptions are not treated as income in such organisations
Because the organisation does not keep complete double-entry records, so assets and liabilities must be listed to estimate the opening fund
Because the organisation has no fixed assets to disclose
questions.e: Many clubs keep only single-entry or incomplete records, so a Statement of Affairs lists assets and liabilities to estimate the opening accumulated fund by difference. This fund then serves as the starting point similar to capital for a trader.
questions.p: Because many clubs no dey keep full double-entry records, dem dey use Statement of Affairs to pack assets and liabilities together. Na so dem take dey find the opening accumulated fund by difference.

questions.q: Okigwe Table Tennis Club bought new equipment costing ₦180,000 during the year, which is to be depreciated at 10% per annum using the straight line method. What is the amount of depreciation to be charged in the Income and Expenditure Account for the year, assuming the equipment was used for the full year?
questions.e: Depreciation is calculated as 10% of the cost of 180,000, which equals 18,000 for the full year. This amount is charged as an expense in the Income and Expenditure Account, reducing the surplus for the year.
questions.p: Depreciation na 10% of the cost wey be ₦180,000 for full year. When you calculate am, you go get ₦18,000 as expense inside the Income and Expenditure Account.

questions.q: Zuma Cultural Club's accounts showed subscriptions in arrears of ₦30,000 at the start of the year and ₦45,000 at the end of the year. Cash received from subscriptions during the year was ₦370,000. There were no subscriptions received in advance. What is the subscription income to be shown in the Income and Expenditure Account?
questions.e: Subscription income for the year equals cash received plus closing arrears minus opening arrears, that is 370,000 plus 45,000 minus 30,000, which equals 385,000. This adjusts cash received to reflect amounts actually earned in the year.
questions.p: To get subscription income, you go add closing arrears to cash wey you receive, then remove opening arrears. That na 370,000 plus 45,000 minus 30,000, wey give you ₦385,000.

questions.q: Emeka and Obi are partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio 3:2. The partnership appropriation account showed net profit of ₦180,000 after charging interest on drawings of ₦10,000 and before charging partners' salary of ₦30,000 to Obi. What amount of profit is available for distribution between the partners?
questions.e: Obi's salary of ₦30,000 is deducted from the net profit of ₦180,000 before sharing the remainder, leaving ₦150,000 for distribution in the profit-sharing ratio. Interest on drawings has already been accounted for in arriving at the ₦180,000.
questions.p: Since the ₦180,000 profit don already include interest on drawings, we just need to remove the ₦30,000 salary. The remaining ₦150,000 na wetin dem go share between the partners.

questions.q: A new partner, Kemi, is admitted into a partnership and agrees to pay a premium for goodwill. If the goodwill account is not to remain permanently in the books, the premium brought in by Kemi should be credited to the old partners' capital accounts in what ratio?
o: The sacrificing ratio of the old partners
Equal ratio regardless of old ratio
The ratio of capital contributed by old partners
The new profit-sharing ratio
questions.e: When goodwill is not retained in the books, the premium paid by the incoming partner is shared among old partners in the sacrificing ratio, which reflects the proportion of profit share each old partner gives up. This compensates the partners who lose more of their share.
questions.p: When new partner pay for goodwill and e no go stay for book, we dey share the money based on how much profit the old partners sacrifice. This one dey make sure say the people wey lose their share get their compensation.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the purpose of a partners' current account in a partnership that maintains fixed capital accounts?
o: To record loans given by partners to the firm
To record the original capital contributed by each partner permanently
To record the partner's share of the cost of goodwill purchased
To record fluctuating items such as salary, interest on capital, drawings and share of profit
questions.e: Where capital accounts are kept fixed, a current account is used to record all other transactions affecting a partner's interest, such as salary, interest on capital, drawings and share of profit or loss. This keeps the capital account balance unchanged except for permanent capital adjustments.
questions.p: If capital account dey fixed, we dey use current account to track all the small-small things like salary, drawings, and profit. This one dey help make the main capital balance no change anyhow.

questions.q: On admission of a new partner, assets are often revalued before the new partner joins. If a revaluation account shows a credit balance of ₦45,000 representing a net gain on revaluation, how should this amount be treated in the books of the old partners?
o: Debited to the goodwill account
Credited to the new partner's capital account
Credited to the old partners' capital accounts in their old profit-sharing ratio
Carried forward as a liability in the balance sheet
questions.e: A profit on revaluation belongs to the old partners since it arose before the new partner was admitted, so it is shared among them in their old profit-sharing ratio and credited to their capital accounts. The new partner does not benefit from gains that occurred before joining.
questions.p: The gain from revaluation na for the old partners because e happen before the new person join. We go share the ₦45,000 among them using their old profit-sharing ratio.

questions.q: Which of the following items would appropriately appear on the debit side of a partner's current account?
o: Share of profit for the year
Drawings made during the year
Salary allowed to the partner
Interest on capital
questions.e: Drawings reduce the amount due to a partner and are therefore debited to the current account. Interest on capital, salary and share of profit all increase the partner's entitlement and are credited instead.
questions.p: Drawings na money wey partner collect from the business, so e dey reduce wetin the business owe them. That is why we dey debit am for the current account.

questions.q: Abiodun and Chika are in partnership with no written agreement. In the absence of a partnership agreement, the Partnership Act provides that partners should share profits and losses in the ratio of:
o: 3:2 in favour of the partner who manages the business
Equal shares
The ratio agreed verbally at the last meeting
The ratio of their capital contributions
questions.e: Where there is no partnership agreement, the law states that profits and losses must be shared equally among all partners, regardless of how much capital each contributed. This is a default rule used to settle disputes.
questions.p: If partnership agreement no dey, law talk say make everybody share profit and loss equal. E no matter how much money each person bring put as capital.

questions.q: Which of the following is the main reason why a partnership prepares a profit and loss appropriation account in addition to the normal trading, profit and loss account?
o: To show how the net profit is shared among the partners after adjusting for interest, salaries and commission
To record the revaluation of assets before a new partner is admitted
To calculate the value of goodwill on admission of a new partner
To record the purchase and sale of goods during the year
questions.e: The appropriation account continues from the profit and loss account and shows how the net profit is distributed among partners after charging items such as interest on capital, partners' salaries and interest on drawings. It is a sharing-out account, not a trading record.
questions.p: Appropriation account dey show how dem dey share net profit among partners after dem don settle interest on capital, salary, and interest on drawings. E be sharing-out account, no be trading record.

questions.q: Okon is admitted into a partnership owned by Essien and Umoh who previously shared profits in the ratio 3:2. After admission, the new profit-sharing ratio becomes Essien 2, Umoh 2 and Okon 1. If the goodwill of the firm is valued at ₦150,000 and is not to remain in the books, the amount Okon should pay as his share of goodwill, to be shared by the old partners in their sacrificing ratio, is:
questions.e: Okon's share of goodwill = (1/5) of 150,000 = 30,000, since his new profit share is 1 out of a total of 5 parts (2+2+1). This amount is credited to the old partners based on how much profit share each sacrificed.
questions.p: Okon share of goodwill na (1/5) of 150,000 wey be 30,000, because hin new profit share na 1 out of 5 total parts. Dem go give old partners this money based on how much profit share each person sacrifice.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why goodwill is usually valued and adjusted in the books when a new partner is admitted into a partnership?
o: To reduce the amount of tax payable by the partnership in that year
To increase the total capital available to the business for expansion
To determine the new partner's salary for the following year
To compensate the old partners for the reputation and future benefits the new partner will enjoy without having built them up
questions.e: Goodwill represents the value built up by the old partners through years of effort, reputation and customer loyalty. When a new partner joins and shares in future profits, goodwill is valued and adjusted so the old partners are fairly compensated for what they are giving up.
questions.p: Goodwill represent the name and market value wey old partners don build over years with hard work. When new partner join, dem must value am so old partners go chop compensation for the future benefit wey the new person dey come met.

questions.q: Ngozi's current account had a debit balance of ₦8,000 at the start of the year. During the year, her share of profit was ₦42,000, interest on capital credited was ₦6,000, and she made drawings of ₦30,000. What is the balance on Ngozi's current account at the end of the year?
o: ₦18,000 credit
₦8,000 debit
₦26,000 credit
₦10,000 credit
questions.e: Start with a debit balance of 8,000, add credits of 42,000 profit share and 6,000 interest on capital, then deduct drawings of 30,000: -8,000 + 42,000 + 6,000 - 30,000 = 10,000, which is a credit balance. A debit opening balance reduces the final credit balance.
questions.p: You go start with debit balance of 8,000, add 42,000 profit and 6,000 interest on capital, then remove 30,000 drawings. When you calculate am well, you go get 10,000 credit balance.

questions.q: Which of the following is a true statement about shares and debentures of a public limited company?
o: A debenture holder is a creditor of the company while a shareholder is a part owner
Both debenture holders and shareholders are owners of the company
Debenture holders receive dividends while shareholders receive interest
Shareholders are entitled to a fixed return whether or not profit is made
questions.e: A debenture is a loan to the company, so its holder is a creditor entitled to fixed interest regardless of profit. A shareholder is a part owner entitled to dividend only when profit is declared.
questions.p: Debenture holder na creditor wey dey collect fixed interest, whether company make profit or not. But shareholder na part-owner wey dey collect dividend only when profit show.

questions.q: Okiki Plc issued 80,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each at par. The shares were fully subscribed and all application money was received. What is the total amount received from the share issue?
questions.e: Shares issued at par means the issue price equals the nominal value of ₦1 per share. Total proceeds equal 80,000 shares multiplied by ₦1, which is ₦80,000.
questions.p: When dem issue shares at par, e mean say the price equal the nominal value of ₦1 per share. So, 80,000 shares multiply by ₦1 go give you ₦80,000.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why a company issues shares at a premium?
o: The premium represents interest owed to shareholders before trading begins
The company is forced by law to charge extra on every share issued
The shares are sold above their nominal value because the company's prospects are strong
The shares are sold below their nominal value to attract more investors
questions.e: A share premium arises when a company is able to sell shares for more than their nominal value, usually because investors have confidence in its performance and future prospects. This premium is credited to a share premium account, a capital reserve.
questions.p: Company dey issue shares at a premium when people want buy am pass the nominal value because the company market value dey sweet. Dem dey keep dis extra money for share premium account as capital reserve.

questions.q: Garuba Holdings Ltd forfeited 2,000 ordinary shares of ₦4 each on which only the application and allotment money of ₦3 per share had been paid. The call money of ₦1 per share was not paid by the defaulting shareholder. What amount should be debited to the Share Capital account on forfeiture?
questions.e: On forfeiture, the full nominal value called up on the shares is removed from Share Capital account. This is 2,000 shares multiplied by ₦4 nominal value, giving ₦8,000.
questions.p: For forfeiture, you must remove the full nominal value wey dem call up from Share Capital account. Na 2,000 shares multiply by ₦4 nominal value, wey give us ₦8,000.

questions.q: Which of the following items would appropriately be transferred to a revenue reserve rather than a capital reserve?
o: Profit on revaluation of a freehold property
Share premium account balance
Undistributed portion of trading profit kept for future dividends
Proceeds from the sale of forfeited shares above nominal value
questions.e: Revenue reserves come from trading profits retained in the business and are available for future dividend distribution. Share premium and revaluation surpluses are capital reserves that are generally not available for dividends.
questions.p: Revenue reserve na trading profit wey company keep for future dividend distribution. Share premium and revaluation surplus na capital reserve wey you no fit use share dividend.

questions.q: Amaka Agro-Allied Plc has in issue 30,000 12% preference shares of ₦10 each and 150,000 ordinary shares of ₦2 each. The directors propose a total dividend payout of ₦72,000 for the year. After paying the preference dividend in full, what amount is available for ordinary shareholders?
questions.e: Preference dividend equals 12% of (30,000 multiplied by ₦10), which is 12% of ₦300,000 = ₦36,000. Subtracting this from the total payout of ₦72,000 leaves ₦36,000 for ordinary shareholders.
questions.p: Preference dividend na 12% of ₦300,000, wey be ₦36,000. When you subtract am from the total ₦72,000 payout, na ₦36,000 remain for ordinary shareholders.

questions.q: A limited liability company wishes to raise long-term capital without diluting the ownership control of existing shareholders. Which of the following sources of finance best achieves this?
o: Issue of debentures to investors
Issue of preference shares convertible to ordinary shares
Issue of additional ordinary shares to the public
Capitalisation of the general reserve into bonus shares
questions.e: Debentures are loan capital, so debenture holders become creditors, not members of the company, leaving voting control of existing shareholders unaffected. Issuing more ordinary shares or convertible preference shares can dilute control over time.
questions.p: Debentures na loan capital, so debenture holders na creditors and dem no get voting power. Dis one mean say existing shareholders go maintain dia control without anybody share power with dem.

questions.q: Sango Industries Plc has a Share Premium account balance of ₦150,000. Which of the following uses of this balance is permitted under standard company accounting practice?
o: Paying directors' salaries for the year
Paying cash dividends to ordinary shareholders
Writing off preliminary expenses incurred on company formation
Covering a trading loss for the year
questions.e: Share premium, being a capital reserve, can only be used for specific purposes allowed by law, such as writing off formation (preliminary) expenses, issuing bonus shares, or writing off issue expenses. It cannot be used to pay dividends or cover trading losses.
questions.p: Share premium na capital reserve wey law allow make you use am write off preliminary expenses or issue bonus shares. You no fit use am pay dividend or cover trading loss.

questions.q: In joint venture accounting, when each co-venturer keeps records only of their own transactions and no separate set of books is opened for the venture, the account prepared by each party to record the venture transactions is called:
o: Joint venture account
Realisation account
Joint bank account
Memorandum joint venture account
questions.e: When no separate books are kept, each co-venturer records the venture's transactions in a Joint Venture Account in his own books, usually alongside a Memorandum Joint Venture Account to find overall profit. The account recording his own entries directly is the Joint Venture Account.
questions.p: If dem no open separate book for di venture, every person go record wetin concern am for im own Joint Venture Account. Dem dey use Memorandum Joint Venture Account join all di record together to see di total profit.

questions.q: Tunde and Bello entered a joint venture to buy and sell bags of rice, sharing profits and losses equally. Tunde bought rice for ₦900,000 and paid transport of ₦60,000. Bello sold all the rice for ₦1,200,000 and paid storage charges of ₦40,000. What is each co-venturer's share of the profit on the venture?
questions.e: Total cost is 900,000 + 60,000 + 40,000 = 1,000,000, and sales are 1,200,000, giving a total profit of 200,000. Shared equally, each co-venturer gets 100,000.
questions.p: Total cost na 1,000,000 and total sales na 1,200,000, so di profit na 200,000. Since dem dey share am equally, each person go get 100,000.

questions.q: A business sends goods to its branch and records both the goods sent and the branch's stock at selling price in the Branch Stock Account, in order to find stock shortages or surpluses easily. This method of branch accounting is best described as the:
o: Debtors system
Stock and debtors system
Wholesale branch system
Final accounts system
questions.e: Under the stock and debtors system, separate accounts are kept for branch stock (at selling price) and branch debtors, which helps reveal any stock shortage or surplus at the branch. This is more detailed than the simple debtors system.
questions.p: For stock and debtors system, dem dey keep separate account for branch stock and debtors. Dis one dey help dem see quick-quick if stock dey missing or if e surplus.

questions.q: Ibeh Traders operates a branch in Enugu and sends all goods to the branch at cost plus 20% mark-up. During the year, goods invoiced to the branch at selling price amounted to ₦720,000. What is the amount of the loading (mark-up) included in the goods sent to the branch?
questions.e: Since cost plus 20% gives the invoice price, cost represents 100/120 of 720,000, which is 600,000, so the loading is 720,000 minus 600,000, that is 120,000. Candidates who wrongly take 20% of 720,000 directly get a distractor answer.
questions.p: Di invoice price na cost plus 20% mark-up, so 720,000 na 120%. To find di loading, you go calculate 20/120 of 720,000, wey be 120,000.

questions.q: In departmental accounts, rent and rates for a shop occupied by several departments are usually apportioned among the departments on the basis of:
o: Purchases made by each department
Sales value of each department
Floor space or area occupied by each department
Number of employees in each department
questions.e: Rent and rates relate to the premises occupied, so the fairest basis for sharing them is the floor space or area used by each department. Sales or purchases figures are not directly related to space used.
questions.p: Rent and rates na money for di space wey you dey use. Na why dem dey share am based on how much floor space each department dey occupy.

questions.q: A head office sends goods to its branch at an invoice price which includes a profit margin. At the end of the year, unsold branch stock at invoice price is ₦250,000, and goods are invoiced at a margin of 25% on selling price. What is the amount of unrealised profit (provision for unrealised profit) included in the closing branch stock?
questions.e: Since the margin is 25% on selling price, the profit element in the stock is simply 25% of 250,000, which equals 62,500. This provision is deducted so only the true cost value of unsold stock is shown in the combined accounts.
questions.p: Since di margin na 25% of di selling price, you just calculate 25% of 250,000. Dis one go give you 62,500 as di unrealised profit wey dey inside di stock.

questions.q: Okoro and Eze agreed to carry out a joint venture in buying and selling second-hand vehicles, without forming a partnership and without keeping a separate set of joint books. Which of the following is the most important reason for preparing a Memorandum Joint Venture Account in such a case?
o: To record cash received from customers by each venturer
To show the total assets owned by the venture at year end
To replace the need for each venturer to record his own transactions
To ascertain the overall profit or loss of the venture and each party's share, since each keeps separate records
questions.e: Because no joint set of books exists and each venturer records only his own transactions, a Memorandum Joint Venture Account combines both sides' figures to calculate the total profit or loss and each person's agreed share. It does not replace each venturer's personal records.
questions.p: Because each person dey record only im own side, dem need Memorandum Joint Venture Account to join everything together. Na so dem go take know di total profit and how much each person go collect.

questions.q: Adaeze Enterprises has two departments, Textiles and Provisions. Total wages for the year were ₦480,000, and the business decided to apportion wages between departments based on the number of workers in each, since both departments pay similar wage rates. Textiles has 9 workers while Provisions has 6 workers. What amount of wages should be charged to the Provisions department?
questions.e: There are 15 workers in total, so Provisions' share is 6 out of 15 of the total wages. This gives 6/15 multiplied by 480,000, which equals 192,000.
questions.p: Total workers na 15, so Provisions department get 6 out of 15. If you calculate 6/15 of 480,000, you go get 192,000 for dem.

questions.q: Which of these best describes the Consolidated Revenue Fund in Nigerian public sector accounting?
o: The main account into which virtually all government revenues are paid before authorized withdrawals
A reserve fund that state governments cannot access
A special fund used only for foreign loan repayments
A fund set aside strictly for paying salaries of civil servants only
questions.e: The Consolidated Revenue Fund is the general pool into which most government revenues are paid. Withdrawals from it require proper legislative authorisation, usually through an Appropriation Act.
questions.p: Consolidated Revenue Fund na di main pot wey all government money dey enter before dem spend am. Before dem fit withdraw money from inside, dem must get proper approval from di law makers.

questions.q: A local government in Kogi State generated internally generated revenue (IGR) of ₦18,000,000 and received statutory allocation of ₦42,000,000 in a given month. If total recurrent expenditure for the month was ₦50,000,000, what was the surplus or deficit for the month?
o: Deficit of ₦10,000,000
Deficit of ₦8,000,000
Surplus of ₦60,000,000
Surplus of ₦10,000,000
questions.e: Total revenue is 18,000,000 + 42,000,000 = 60,000,000. Subtracting expenditure of 50,000,000 gives a surplus of 10,000,000.
questions.p: If you add 18,000,000 and 42,000,000, you go get 60,000,000 as total revenue. When you remove di 50,000,000 wey dem spend, you go remain with 10,000,000 surplus.

questions.q: The accounting officer in a Nigerian government ministry who is primarily responsible and answerable to the Public Accounts Committee for the proper use of public funds is the:
o: Auditor-General
Permanent Secretary
Accountant-General
Minister of Finance
questions.e: The Permanent Secretary, as the accounting officer of a ministry, is personally responsible for ensuring funds are properly used and must appear before the Public Accounts Committee to explain spending.
questions.p: Permanent Secretary na di person wey dem call accounting officer for ministry. Na im get responsibility to explain how dem take spend money if Public Accounts Committee call am.

questions.q: Which independent officer is constitutionally empowered to examine and report on the accounts of all government ministries and departments in Nigeria, without being controlled by the executive arm?
o: Accountant-General of the Federation
Director of Budget
Auditor-General for the Federation
Chief Internal Auditor
questions.e: The Auditor-General for the Federation is an independent officer who audits government accounts and reports to the National Assembly, ensuring checks on how public funds are spent.
questions.p: Auditor-General for the Federation na di person wey get power to check all government account. E no dey under executive control and e dey report wetin e see straight to National Assembly.

questions.q: A Federal Ministry's final accounts showed total recurrent revenue of ₦75,000,000, recurrent expenditure of ₦48,000,000, capital receipts of ₦20,000,000 and capital expenditure of ₦35,000,000 for the year. What was the overall net position for the year?
o: Overall surplus of ₦27,000,000
Overall deficit of ₦15,000,000
Overall deficit of ₦12,000,000
Overall surplus of ₦12,000,000
questions.e: Recurrent surplus is 75,000,000 - 48,000,000 = 27,000,000, while capital account shows a deficit of 35,000,000 - 20,000,000 = 15,000,000. Combining both gives an overall surplus of 27,000,000 - 15,000,000 = 12,000,000.
questions.p: Recurrent surplus na 27,000,000, but capital account get 15,000,000 deficit. When you subtract di deficit from di surplus, you go get 12,000,000 overall surplus.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major limitation of cash basis accounting as used in the Nigerian public sector, compared with accrual accounting?
o: It automatically overstates government assets every year
It fails to show outstanding liabilities and amounts owed to government, since only actual cash movements are recorded
It makes budgeting completely impossible for government
It requires government to maintain two separate sets of books at all times
questions.e: Under cash basis accounting, transactions are recorded only when cash changes hands, so debts owed to or by government (like unpaid bills or revenue due but uncollected) do not appear in the accounts, giving an incomplete picture of financial position.
questions.p: Cash basis accounting only dey record money when e don enter or comot from hand. Because of dis, e no dey show money wey government still owe or money wey people owe government, so di account no dey complete.

questions.q: Under the weighted average method of stock valuation, the cost per unit is calculated by:
o: Dividing total cost of goods available for sale by total units available for sale
Dividing total sales value by total units sold
Taking the cost of the most recent purchase only
Taking the cost of the earliest purchase only
questions.e: The weighted average cost per unit is found by dividing the total cost of goods available for sale by the total number of units available for sale. This gives one average cost applied to both closing stock and cost of sales.
questions.p: To get weighted average cost, you go divide total cost of goods wey dey available by total units wey dey available. This one go give you one average price wey you go use for closing stock and cost of sales.

questions.q: A key argument in favour of using the FIFO method of stock valuation is that it:
o: Always produces the lowest profit figure during inflation
Matches current sales revenue with current purchase costs
Reduces the amount of tax payable during periods of rising prices
Values closing stock at prices closest to current replacement cost
questions.e: Under FIFO, closing stock consists of the most recently purchased items, so its value is close to current market or replacement prices. This makes the balance sheet figure for stock more realistic.
questions.p: FIFO method dey assume say the goods wey you buy first na im you sell first. Because of this, the closing stock wey remain na the ones wey you buy last, so the value dey close to current market price.

questions.q: During a period of persistently falling prices, which stock valuation method will usually produce the HIGHEST value for closing stock?
o: LIFO
Marginal Costing
Weighted Average
FIFO
questions.e: When prices are falling, LIFO leaves the earlier, more expensive purchases in closing stock because the cheaper recent purchases are treated as sold first. This gives LIFO a higher closing stock value than FIFO in a falling price situation, which is the reverse of what happens when prices rise.
questions.p: If price dey fall, LIFO go keep the old expensive goods for stock because e dey assume say the cheap new ones don sell finish. This one make the closing stock value high pass wetin FIFO go give.

questions.q: Bosede Trading Company has a gross profit of ₦180,000 and sales of ₦900,000 for the year ended 31 December. What is the gross profit margin?
questions.e: Gross profit margin is gross profit divided by sales, multiplied by 100. This gives 180,000/900,000 x 100 = 20%.
questions.p: To find gross profit margin, you go divide gross profit by sales, then multiply am by 100. If you do 180,000 divided by 900,000 times 100, e go give you 20%.

questions.q: A company's directors want to assess how efficiently the business uses its assets to generate sales. Which ratio would best help them answer this question?
o: Debt-equity ratio
Asset turnover ratio
Gross profit margin
Current ratio
questions.e: Asset turnover ratio measures how well a business uses its assets to generate sales revenue. It is calculated as sales divided by total assets, showing efficiency in asset usage rather than profitability or liquidity.
questions.p: Asset turnover ratio dey show how well company dey use im property and assets to make sales. E dey measure efficiency, no be profit or how cash flow tight.

questions.q: Okafor Supplies has current assets of ₦350,000, including stock of ₦110,000, and current liabilities of ₦140,000. Calculate the acid test (quick) ratio.
questions.e: Quick assets exclude stock, so quick assets equal 350,000 minus 110,000 = 240,000. Dividing by current liabilities of 140,000 gives approximately 1.7:1.
questions.p: For quick ratio, you must remove stock from current assets first. When you minus 110,000 stock from 350,000, you get 240,000, and when you divide am by 140,000 current liabilities, e go give you 1.7:1.

questions.q: A supermarket's management notices that its rate of stock turnover has fallen sharply compared to last year, although sales figures remain almost the same. Which of the following best explains this situation?
o: The business is holding more stock relative to sales than before
The business is selling goods faster than before
The business has improved its profit margin significantly
The business has reduced its credit period to customers
questions.e: A falling stock turnover rate with similar sales means stock is moving more slowly, which happens when a business holds more average stock than before. This ties up funds and may signal overstocking or slow-moving goods.
questions.p: If stock turnover rate drop but sales remain the same, e mean say goods dey stay long for warehouse before dem sell am. Na because business dey carry more stock pass normal.

questions.q: Which of the following ratios is most useful to a bank considering whether to grant a long-term loan to a company?
o: Debtors collection period
Gross profit margin
Gearing (leverage) ratio
Stock turnover ratio
questions.e: Gearing ratio compares long-term debt to equity capital, showing how much a company relies on borrowed funds. A bank uses this to judge the risk of lending more money to the business.
questions.p: Gearing ratio dey compare long-term debt with company equity. Bank need am to know whether person fit borrow long-term money without wahala.

questions.q: Tunde Motors reported net profit after tax of ₦240,000 and ordinary share capital plus reserves of ₦1,600,000 at year end. Calculate the return on equity.
questions.e: Return on equity equals net profit after tax divided by shareholders' funds, multiplied by 100. This gives 240,000/1,600,000 x 100 = 15%.
questions.p: Return on equity na net profit after tax divided by shareholders fund, times 100. If you calculate 240,000 over 1,600,000 times 100, e go give you 15%.

questions.q: A company's current ratio is 3:1, but its acid test ratio is only 0.8:1. Which of the following is the most likely explanation?
o: A large proportion of current assets is tied up in stock
The company's creditors exceed its debtors
The company has very little stock on hand
The company has no current liabilities
questions.e: A big gap between the current ratio and acid test ratio shows that stock forms a large part of current assets. Removing stock for the acid test sharply reduces the ratio, suggesting possible liquidity difficulty if stock cannot be sold quickly.
questions.p: If current ratio high but acid test ratio low, e mean say stock plenty inside current assets. If stock no sell quick, cash flow fit enter inside trouble.

questions.q: Ijeoma Stores had credit purchases of ₦960,000 during the year and trade creditors of ₦160,000 at year end. Using a 365-day year, calculate the average period of credit taken from suppliers.
o: 45 days
50 days
90 days
61 days
questions.e: Creditors' payment period equals trade creditors divided by credit purchases, multiplied by 365. This gives 160,000/960,000 x 365, which is approximately 61 days.
questions.p: To find creditor payment period, you divide trade creditors by credit purchases and multiply am by 365 days. Doing 160,000 over 960,000 times 365 go give you about 61 days.
